item.content:encoded:
Tech Community AI Digest 2026-10-26

Sources: Dev.to (30 articles) + Lobste.rs (7 stories) | Generated: 2026-10-26 00:37 UTC

Tech Community AI Digest — 2026-10-26

1. Today’s Highlights

Dev.to’s AI feed is dominated by the Hacktoberfest “Slow and Steady” challenge, with many posts building local, Gemma-powered agents for email, screenshots, spending, research, and other everyday workflows—often with a playful sloth theme. The more production-minded discussions focus on testing LLM-assisted code, agent evaluation and citation integrity, and AI cost/ownership postmortems. A recurring serving lesson is that KV-cache/context memory, not just model weights, limits LLM concurrency, while teams are adopting “model proposes, deterministic code verifies” patterns. On Lobste.rs, AI attention is smaller but broader: Mistral’s time-series foundation models, PyTorch backward-pass security research, EU data/privacy controversy, and new coarse-to-fine text-generation research.

2. Dev.to Highlights

Article Reactions Comments Summary
Three Times My Test Failed and the LLM Was Right 20 20 A test failure is not automatically a code bug; an LLM can reveal flawed assumptions in tests and expected behavior. Use LLM feedback as a debugging partner, but verify each claim against code and test intent.
Postmortem: The Tuesday Our AI Bill Had No Owner 7 3 An AI bill without a clear owner exposes gaps in cost visibility, budget guards, and incident response. The postmortem is useful for teams adding AI spend controls before finance or reliability incidents.
How Machines Find Meaning: The Math Behind Semantic Search 6 0 Explains cosine similarity and Euclidean distance for semantic search in developer-friendly math. Useful foundation for reasoning about embeddings, retrieval quality, and RAG systems.
I OOM'd on 100 Rows Because One File Was 590 MB 5 2 A 100-row job can still exhaust memory when one input file is hundreds of MB. The lesson is to stream/lazy-load data, inspect file sizes, and test realistic payloads rather than row counts alone.
LitPivot makes a quiet research bug visible: the metric can outlive the idea 5 0 Research metrics can silently outlive the hypothesis they were designed to test. Treat evaluation dashboards as code to review when ideas change, or teams may optimize stale signals.
How to Integrate Investment Research into Your AI Agent 5 1 Walks through adding investment-research data to an AI agent via an API. Useful as a concrete tool-integration and data-grounding pattern for finance-adjacent agents.
Why the KV cache, not the weights, decides how many users an LLM server can hold 3 4 LLM serving capacity is often constrained by KV-cache memory as context length and concurrency grow, not just model weights. Capacity planning should model token context, batching, and concurrency together.
My HVAC Voice Agent Was Listening for the Word Invisalign 2 1 A voice-agent bug appeared as the system listening for an unrelated word, showing why exported config diffs and transcript tests matter. Voice agents need intent, prompt/config, and ASR error testing—not just text-chat evals.
One Agent Framework Seemed to Lose Half Its Citations. Most Were Just Reformatted. 1 0 Apparent citation loss in agent evaluations may be normalization or reformatting rather than true hallucination. Inspect raw outputs and use robust citation matching before declaring an agent unreliable.
The Model Proposes, Rust Verifies: Triaging Job Postings with a Local Gemma 1 0 Uses a local Gemma model to propose job-postings triage while Rust enforces deterministic checks. This is a reusable reliability pattern: let models generate, but validate with code.

3. Lobste.rs Highlights

Story Score Comments Summary
Unikernels in OCaml · discuss 64 16 Top-scoring Lobsters item: a site about building unikernels in OCaml. Worth reading for systems/runtime design and as a signal of strong interest in minimal, language-centric infrastructure—though it is not AI-specific.
Timestral: Mistral's time-series foundation models · discuss 10 1 Mistral introduces foundation models aimed at time-series forecasting. Relevant for teams considering pretrained forecasting models instead of bespoke statistical pipelines.
ConcurrentML: Improving on Go's concurrency model · discuss 10 5 Explores ConcurrentML ideas as an alternative concurrency model to Go’s goroutines and channels. Useful for developers thinking about composable concurrency primitives, though it is not an AI story.
How to Run Turing-Complete Malware in PyTorch's Backward Pass · discuss 6 1 Shows how PyTorch’s backward pass can be abused to run Turing-complete malware, raising ML supply-chain and model-execution security questions. Read it before loading untrusted models or custom autograd code.
Next-Concept Modeling: Fast, Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation · discuss 3 0 Proposes fast, parallel coarse-to-fine text generation instead of strictly sequential token decoding. Worth reading for LLM inference research and alternative generation architectures.
AI: EU Member States approve “digital expropriation” of Europeans for AI companies · discuss 0 0 noyb reports that EU member states approved what it calls “digital expropriation” of Europeans’ data for AI companies. Important context for privacy, training-data compliance, and AI regulation.
Trees to Flows and Back: Unifying Decision Trees and Diffusion Models · discuss 0 0 Explores a theoretical unification between decision trees and diffusion models. Relevant for researchers interested in generative modeling, interpretability, and hybrid model families.

4. Community Pulse

Across both platforms, the practical mood is less “what can AI do?” and more “how do we keep it observable, cheap, and correct?” Dev.to’s Hacktoberfest wave is full of local Gemma/open-model agents for email, screenshots, spending, and research, often with a deterministic validator or local-first constraint. The strongest posts focus on evaluation failures: tests that reveal model reasoning, citation loss that is really reformatting, stale research metrics, and voice-agent config bugs. Developers are also confronting production realities—AI bills without an owner, KV-cache pressure on LLM concurrency, memory blowups from oddly large input files, and the need to inspect raw model I/O. Common emerging patterns include “model proposes, code verifies,” streaming/lazy data handling, budget ownership, retrieval math, and transcript/config diffs for agents. Lobste.rs adds a security and policy lens—PyTorch execution risks, EU data/privacy fights, and time-series foundation models—while its top overall discussion remains systems-language infrastructure.

5. Worth Reading

  • Three Times My Test Failed and the LLM Was Right — the best practical Dev.to read on using LLM feedback to challenge test assumptions rather than blindly changing code.
  • Postmortem: The Tuesday Our AI Bill Had No Owner — strongest production/governance piece in the Dev.to set; useful for engineering leaders and SREs adding AI cost controls.
  • How to Run Turing-Complete Malware in PyTorch's Backward Pass · discuss — a security-minded read for anyone loading models or custom autograd code; pairs well with agent/tool supply-chain concerns.

This digest is auto-generated by agents-radar.

item.content:encoded:
AI CLI 工具社区动态日报 2026-10-25

生成时间: 2026-10-25 00:29 UTC | 覆盖工具: 7 个

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code
  • Claude Code Skills

横向对比

跨工具对比：AI CLI 开发者工具 — 2026-10-25

1. 生态概览

2026-10-25 的各份摘要显示，市场正从能力演示转向运营信任。Claude Code 正处于明显的维护低谷，套餐层级需求高度一致，但沙箱数据丢失报告仍未解决；Codex 则集中于 Windows/app-server 稳定性与 MCP 资源隔离。Gemini CLI、OpenCode、Pi、Copilot CLI 和 Qwen Code 都在围绕智能体编排、资源生命周期、配额/认证正确性和平台一致性进行迭代。在各社区中，核心问题已不再是“智能体能不能写代码？”，而是“它能否可靠完成、安全恢复并如实汇报？”企业采购信号——Claude Team 20x、Copilot 计费事件、Qwen CI/运行时自动化——正日益显著。

2. 活动对比

下表计数为摘要所报告的 24 小时窗口内数据，并非完整仓库总量。“Notable/listed（值得注意/已列出）”指摘要中明确剖析的条目。n/d = 摘要未提供计数。N/A 仅用于已禁用的社区渠道；本数据集中这七款工具均未在上游禁用 Issues/PRs。

工具 Issues 数 PR 数 Discussions 数 发布状态
Claude Code 50 条更新；10 条已剖析 2 条更新；0 条合并 n/d 无发布
OpenAI Codex 10 条值得注意；总数 n/r 0 条更新 10 条已剖析（8 条展示分享，2 条问答） 无发布
Gemini CLI 14 条值得注意（10 条热门 + 4 条关注） 14 条列出（10 条关键 + 4 条其他） n/d 1 个每日构建（v0.67.0-nightly.20261024）
GitHub Copilot CLI 20 条更新 0 条更新 n/d 2 个补丁（v1.0.104-2、v1.0.104-3）
OpenCode 13 条值得注意；引用 ≥12 条配额报告（有重叠） 16 条列出（10 条关键 + 6 条其他） n/d 无发布
Pi 12 条值得注意 10 条列出 2 条已剖析 无发布
Qwen Code 13 条值得注意 15 条列出（10 条关键 + 5 条其他） n/d 2 个发布（v0.26.1、desktop-v0.26.1）

如何解读表格： Claude 的 Issue 窗口最广，单一 Issue 互动也最强，但已合并 PR 活动为零。Gemini、Qwen、OpenCode 和 Pi 的代码审查吞吐更密集。Codex 和 Copilot 的“0 条 PR 更新”数字属于快照限制或 PR 可见性偏低，并不证明没有工作在进行。

3. 共同功能方向

七项跨工具需求在多个社区中反复出现：

  1. 真实的智能体状态与终止语义

    • Gemini： 在 MAX_TURNS 下误报 GOAL 成功，以及浏览器失败（#22323、#21983、#29779）。
    • Codex： 有证据支撑的完成报告（#36718）。
    • Copilot： 子智能体工具静默丢失与上下文轮转损坏（#5243、#5205）。
    • OpenCode： 父智能体收不到后续子智能体回合（#58825）。
    • Qwen： 因 429 被误分类而跳过回退链（#13895）。
    • 需求： 明确的成功/失败原因、证据映射、父子结果传播，以及可审计的完成声明。

  2. 后台/并行任务生命周期与资源隔离

    • Copilot： 后台 shell 完成事件破坏回合（#4946）、inotify 耗尽（#5242）、上下文轮转失败（#5205）。
    • Codex： 每线程 MCP 进程爆炸（#53285）、git diff 扇出（#43019）、临时线程泄漏 MCP 栈（#39783）。
    • OpenCode： 有界关闭（#58817）、后台子智能体汇报（#58825）。
    • Pi： 流式输出期间 TUI 占满全部核心（#6665、#7730）。
    • 需求： 有界进程并发、清理/回收、超时、背压和优雅关闭。

  3. 配额、计费与认证一致性

    • Claude： Team 计划需要等同 Max-20x 的层级（#47509）。
    • Codex： 使用上限重置未跨客户端识别（#51043）。
    • Copilot： Assisted Permissions PRU 耗尽事件（#4802）。
    • OpenCode： 免费层级配额永不重置；86,400 秒循环（#58830、#58831、#58827）。
    • Qwen： 推理 token 在成本显示中被重复计算（#15444）。
    • Pi： 使用上限中断/恢复工作流（#11306）。
    • 需求： 可预测的权益状态、跨客户端同步、准确的 token 核算，以及透明的重置语义。

  4. 权限/沙箱信任与同意

    • Claude： 破坏性沙箱文件系统操作（#93287、#93408）以及不一致的自动模式分类器（#101327）。
    • Gemini： 沙箱化优先于限制（#19873）、破坏性命令护栏（#22672）。
    • OpenCode： 权限“询问”静默允许编辑/写入（#58527）。
    • Copilot： ACP OAuth 刷新与浏览器重定向冲突（#5229）。
    • Codex： 沙箱/权限状态不透明。
    • 需求： 确定性审批、清晰可读的沙箱边界、工具扩展时重新征得同意、安全默认值，以及试运行/恢复路径。

  5. 提供商/模型路由与互操作性

    • Pi： 大规模提供商扩展 PR 链（#11368–#11372）、Gemini 思维签名（#10157）、Bedrock 图像载荷（#8643）。
    • OpenCode： v1→v2 配置不匹配（#58533）、过期模型污染目录（#57931）。
    • Qwen： 严格的 OpenAI 兼容工具 schema（#12222）、429 回退分类（#13895）。
    • Gemini： 作用域内工具过多导致 400（#24246）。
    • Codex： 模型路由不透明与静默模型切换。
    • 需求： 声明式模型目录、能力感知路由、优雅回退，以及适配器级一致性测试。

  6. 上下文、记忆连续性与压缩

    • OpenCode： 手动压缩可能永久损坏会话（#58724）。
    • Qwen： 会话记录快照索引上限导致会话无法打开（#13113）。
    • Codex： AGENTS.md 传播检查与跨新会话的决策图。
    • Pi： 扩展排序丢失 Anthropic system 字段（#11157）、嵌入式会话记忆保留（#10642）。
    • Gemini： 持久化基于文件的任务状态（#18836）。
    • 需求： 持久会话存储、可恢复压缩、上下文交接，以及跨项目记忆隔离。

  7. 终端/桌面/无头模式一致性

    • Claude： 桌面端提示建议、插件渲染钩子、Remote Control 持久化。
    • Codex： Windows VS Code 启动、iPad 远程会话、Windows MCP 进程计数。
    • Gemini： Wayland 浏览器子智能体失败、OSC 7501 终端状态。
    • Copilot： Windows 代理/STT、ACP 一致性、本地 Web UI 请求。
    • OpenCode： Windows %temp% 重定位、跨卷二进制文件保留。
    • Pi： Ctrl+Shift+C 提示丢失、Windows CSI 泄漏、Alacritty 输入法。
    • Qwen： Web Shell i18n 回退阻挡非英语浏览器。
    • 需求： 跨平台 CI 矩阵、无头模式一致性、可访问的 UI 回退，以及终端原生状态报告。

4. 差异化分析

工具 功能重点 目标用户 技术路线
Claude Code Team 计划分层、桌面/TUI 打磨、沙箱安全、插件渲染、Remote Control 团队、企业采购、高级用户 沙箱化 Bash/桌面端、权限分类器、插件 UI 钩子、Remote Control、Max 层级用量模型
OpenAI Codex Windows 桌面端/app-server 稳定性、IDE 扩展、MCP 生命周期、远程/移动端、AGENTS.md Windows/IDE 开发者、通过 ChatGPT 认证的用户、企业应用用户 App-server + VS Code 扩展、MCP、线程/历史 API、有证据支撑的完成方向
Gemini CLI 子智能体可靠性、ACP/编辑器集成、终端原生状态、AST 感知上下文、沙箱化 Google 生态中的终端/编辑器开发者 CLI + ACP、子智能体编排、OSC 7501、AST/工具作用域实验、零依赖沙箱提案
GitHub Copilot CLI Autopilot 异步正确性、SDK/ACP/无头模式、插件技能、企业代理/OAuth GitHub 企业用户、CI/容器用户、Copilot 订阅者 Autopilot、MCP、ACP、插件命名空间、托管模型 fusion、补丁发布节奏
OpenCode 免费层级/桌面端、v2 迁移、提供商互操作、会话完整性 个人开发者、免费层级用户、桌面端/CLI 用户 客户端/服务器会话传输、模型目录 ETag、子智能体、主题、桌面端/CLI 融合
Pi 提供商广度、扩展 API、TUI 性能、嵌入式 SDK、长会话 高级用户、扩展作者、嵌入式/多会话宿主 声明式提供商定义、models.dev 目录、TUI 性能工作、扩展生命周期 API
Qwen Code CI/PR 自动化、运行时代理/Kubernetes、桌面端/守护进程、成本核算 Qwen 生态、自托管/企业 CI 团队 CLI + 守护进程/桌面端、运行时代理、托管智能体、严格的 OpenAI 兼容提供商处理

战略分野在于平台自有的企业级栈——Claude Code、Codex、Copilot CLI 和 Gemini CLI——与生态/扩展性驱动的工具——OpenCode、Pi 和 Qwen Code。前者在集成深度、管理控制和安全方面竞争；后者则在提供商覆盖、定制化和快速迭代方面竞争。

5. 社区动能与成熟度

  • 最高原始互动量： Claude Code 和 Pi。Claude 的 #47509 达到 187 👍 / 67 条评论，其沙箱数据丢失问题簇属于安全关键问题。Pi 的 #4945 有 88 条评论 / 35 👍，表明长会话可靠性存在深层痛点。
  • 强劲的 Issue 接收活动： Copilot CLI（20 个 Issue 更新）、Claude（50 个 Issue 窗口）、OpenCode（配额危机，≥12 份报告）和 Codex（Windows/app-server 问题簇）。这些社区在积极提交，但并非所有社区都获得成比例的合并吞吐。
  • 可见迭代最快： Gemini CLI（每日构建 + 14 个列出的 PR）、Qwen Code（2 个发布 + 15 个列出的 PR）、OpenCode（16 个列出的 PR）和 Pi（堆叠的提供商扩展 PR 链）。这些工具显示维护者正在积极落地正确性、性能和提供商相关工作。
  • 成熟度 vs. 速度： Claude、Codex、Copilot 和 Gemini 拥有更广的功能面和企业采用，但背负平台债——沙箱信任、Windows 稳定性、无头模式一致性、分诊滞后。OpenCode、Pi 和 Qwen 更年轻、迭代更可见，但流程成熟度落后：OpenCode 的权益事件和 Pi 的贡献门禁关闭显示存在运营缺口。
  • 结论： Claude 拥有最具影响力的社区信号，但集成姿态停滞。Gemini、Qwen、OpenCode 和 Pi 迭代最快。Codex 和 Copilot 依然成熟，但受限于 Windows/无头模式可靠性，以及本快照中可见 PR 吞吐偏低。

6. 趋势信号

  1. 可靠性是新的差异化因素。 虚假成功报告、无限挂起、轮转损坏和后台任务损坏在 Gemini、Copilot、OpenCode 和 Pi 中均有出现。采购方应评估终止语义、恢复路径和证据汇报——而不仅仅是模型质量。
  2. 资源隔离正在向上层迁移。 每线程 MCP 进程、git diff 扇出、inotify 耗尽以及 TUI CPU/RAM 增长表明，进程预算、背压和清理如今已是智能体运行时的核心要求。
  3. 计费/认证/配额透明度是一层信任。 配额重置、PRU 耗尽、token 重复计算和计划层级上限都是采用障碍。企业应要求可审计的用量归因和跨客户端状态一致性。
  4. 同意与沙箱可读性比沙箱宣称更重要。 破坏性文件系统操作、静默编辑/写入权限和非确定性分类器会侵蚀信任。显式审批模型、重新征得同意、试运行和文件系统边界正成为基本门槛。
  5. 提供商中立的适配器与回退具有战略意义。 Pi 的提供商扩展、OpenCode 的 v1→v2 迁移痛点、Qwen 的 OpenAI 兼容严格性，以及 Gemini 的工具作用域限制，都指向声明式目录、能力路由和一致性测试。
  6. 无头/CI/容器一致性将成为采购标准。 ACP、OAuth 刷新、代理感知、inotify 限制、Windows 行为和非英语 UI 回退不再是边缘情况——它们决定工具能否在企业 CI 和远程环境中工作。
  7. 智能体可观测性与评估工具正在兴起。 有证据支撑的完成、AGENTS.md 验证、子智能体轨迹可见性，以及基于 pytest 的行为检查，都是围绕智能体信任的新工具层的早期信号。
  8. 社区运营是领先指标。 stale-bot 自动关闭、CI 容量瓶颈、贡献门禁和发布自动化质量，与实质性问题得到解决的速度直接相关。对决策者而言，PR 吞吐和分诊健康度是实用的支持质量信号。

Claude Code 社区摘要 — 2026-10-25

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有发布新版本，PR 队列实际上处于休眠状态（2 个已关闭 PR，0 个值得强调的合并）。社区注意力仍集中在 套餐分层 —— Issue #47509 的 👍 已超过 187，并有 67 条评论要求提供与 Max-20x-equivalent 对等的 Team 席位 —— 以及一对 数据丢失事故报告（#93287、#93408），其中沙箱化的 Bash/Desktop 会话据称删除了 macOS Applications 和主目录内容。与此同时，Desktop Code 标签页继续积累围绕提示建议、插件渲染钩子和 Remote Control 会话持久化的小而高摩擦的回归。

2. 发布

省略——过去 24 小时内未发布任何版本。

3. 热点 Issue

  3. #93408 — Desktop 删除了 macOS 主文件夹内容，包括钥匙串（OPEN，high-priority，data-loss） 与 #93287 相伴的报告，牵涉 Bash + Desktop 的沙箱边界。钥匙串丢失使问题从烦扰升级为安全事件；两者约 6 周后仍处于开启状态。

  5. #102988 — 按状态为侧边栏会话行设置样式（OPEN，enhancement，7 条评论） 请求用整行颜色编码（running / needs-input / unread / cache-expired）取代单一状态圆点。描述清晰；反映出并行 agent 会话已变得多么拥挤。

4. 关键 PR 进展

本时间窗口内仅有 2 个 pull request 更新，二者均为 CLOSED 且均未合并——应将其视为集成停滞的信号，而非功能进展。

  2. #16132 — 修复：/install-github-app 对 dev container 的支持（CLOSED） 修复了一个真实的入门阻碍：在 dev container 内完成 gh 认证后，/install-github-app 仍报告 gh 未认证。通过添加 GitHub CLI 仓库以获取最新 gh 解决。自 1 月起开启。

分析师注： 在零开启 PR、零发布的情况下，社区 Issue 积压的增长速度快于消化速度——这一模式直接体现在第 7 节。

5. 热门讨论

省略——本数据集未提供 Discussions 数据。

6. 功能请求趋势

  • 高级用户套餐分层（B2B）。 #47509 占主导。这一诉求是结构性的：按席位倍数并不能映射 agentic 编码实际消耗 token 的方式，团队想要一个具备管理/计费控制的 20x 级席位。
  • 将 Desktop Code 标签页打造为一流的多 agent 控制台。 一组紧密相关的请求（#102988、#102031、#101312）针对侧边栏信息密度：基于状态的行样式、人类可读的项目文件夹分组名称，以及将文本选择菜单暴露为 ui.render 组件。用户正在运行许多并发会话，而 UI 尚未跟上。
  • 插件/mod API 表面扩展。 #101312 和 #102480 都涉及 ui.render 扩展点（AbovePrompt、选择菜单）。Mod 开发者正把 API 推向 Anthropic 尚未正式定义的布局领域。
  • 终端兼容性与能力协商。 #99566 要求 kitty-graphics 探测信任实际的图形查询响应，而不是将 XTVERSION 字符串与 kitty/ghostty 匹配。基于 SwiftTerm 的终端（Moo）尽管支持 Unicode 占位符，却被排除在外。
  • TUI 人体工学。 #83528 和 #103959 都是小而精确的请求，要求可预测的快捷键和可调整大小的窗格——这项不起眼的工作决定了 CLI 是否显得专业。
  • 退出行为实验。 #89735（closed stale）请求提供一个有文档记录的开关，以禁用静默队列实验；#89860 展示了下游症状：用户对未经请求的模型切换感到惊讶。这是透明度诉求，而非功能诉求。
  • 远程/无头会话可靠性。 #104700 和 #97368 指向一个共同主题：会话状态和通知无法在睡眠/恢复后保留，削弱了手机侧或无人值守操作。
  • 沙箱/安全同意界面。 #89866（closed stale）指出，远程 MCP 服务器可以向已受信任的连接器添加面向外部的工具而无需重新同意——这是安全模型缺口，而非 bug。

7. 开发者痛点

  1. 沙箱会话中的破坏性文件系统操作。 #93287 和 #93408 是急性案例，但底层投诉更广泛：“沙箱”与“真实主目录”之间的信任边界对用户不可读，且事故后恢复没有文档。这是数据集中严重性最高的主题。
  2. 权限分类器不可预测。 #101327 描述了同一操作在不同运行中、在变化的类别下被允许或被阻止。权限层的非确定性迫使用户回到手动批准，这违背了自动模式的目的。
  3. 多 agent 工作流因单次拒绝而中止。 #88216（closed stale）说得很好：在一个工具调用上按 Esc 或 Deny 会终止整个并行运行。对于任何使用 Workflow/并行子 agent 的人来说，这使权限提示的代价不成比例地高。
  4. Desktop 会话存储中的数据完整性回归。 #89497（Windows MSIX 修复清除了 100 个对话中的 97 个）、#89873（.jsonl 完好却显示“No messages yet”）以及 #89871（为从未发生的一轮打上 lastActivityAt 时间戳）描述了一个与自身磁盘真实状态不一致的存储。
  5. 通过队列实验静默改变行为。 工具选择、文件编辑方式（例如用 sed/heredoc 代替 Read/Edit/Write）和系统提示的未宣布变化，破坏了用户预期以及任何固定在先前行为上的提示/评估。
  6. stale-bot 关闭实质性报告。 今天 50 个 Issue 的窗口中很大一部分是 [CLOSED] [stale]——包括安全（#89866）、数据丢失（#89497）和 agent 正确性（#82821）问题。仓库自身的自动化 PR（#62597）仍未合并，因此分类工具似乎正随积压一起衰败。
  7. 安装/更新路径冲突。 #84224（closed，已复现）记录了自动更新器安装到 PATH 解析出的 npm prefix，并在存在多个 Node prefix 时覆盖另一个安装——这是常见的 nvm + Homebrew 配置。与版本无关，因此会再次出现。
  8. 模型路由不透明。 #89876（advisor 选择了与文档不同的模型）和 #89860（“又一次毫无理由的愚蠢切换到 opus 4.8”）表明，用户感觉自己无法控制由哪个模型执行工作，也不喜欢事后才发现。
  9. Desktop 上的通知与连接不稳定。 #97368（间歇性的轮次完成通知）、#89719 和 #83745（在孤儿 claude.exe 进程累积并耗尽命名管道后，Claude-in-Chrome 永久“未连接”）。后者有一个已知的变通方法——杀掉陈旧进程——但这本不应成为必要操作。

2026-10-25 底线： 该仓库正处于维护低谷——没有发布、没有开启的 PR，积压正通过 stale 关闭而非解决来削减。值得关注的两个信号是 Team 20x 档位请求（商业性、高度共识）和 沙箱数据丢失报告（安全关键、当前未解决）。

Gemini CLI 社区摘要 — 2026-10-25

1. 今日亮点

2. 发布

v0.67.0-nightly.20261024.gcd1b45c2d — 发布说明

仅 nightly 构建（本时间窗内无稳定版发布）。可见变更：

  • CLI： 在请求取消后停止继续流处理并自动提示（#29868）——防止 CLI 在用户取消后继续消费/输出。
  • CLI： 修正泰语和老挝语 SARA AM 的显示宽度（#29868-adjacent PR by @elberthc-byte）——针对东南亚文字的终端宽度渲染修复。

3. 热门 Issue

  1. #22323 — P1：子代理 MAX_TURNS 恢复被报告为 GOAL 成功（13 条评论，2 👍）。codebase_investigator 返回 status: "success" / Termination Reason: "GOAL"，尽管其自身输出承认在分析任何内容之前就已达到轮次上限。这是当天评论最多的 issue，因为它破坏了编排语义：调用方无法区分“已完成”和“已放弃”，导致多代理流水线无法验证。

  2. #21409 — P1：通用代理挂起（8 条评论，8 👍——本组中最高反应数）。一旦工作被委派，诸如创建文件夹之类的简单操作就会无限期挂起；用户报告等待长达一小时。变通方法（指示模型不要委派给子代理）实际上禁用了该功能，这解释了社区为何反应强烈。

  3. #19873 — P2：零依赖操作系统沙箱 + 执行后意图路由（9 条评论）。提议让 Gemini 依赖其原生的 bash 亲和力（grep/sed/awk 链），同时通过沙箱而非限制工具来控制风险。值得注意的是，这是对当前工具权限模型的主要架构性反提案。

  4. #21968 — P2：Gemini 没有充分使用技能和子代理（7 条评论）。虽是轶事但引发广泛共鸣：描述清晰的技能（例如 gradle、git）除非显式调用，否则会被忽略。这很重要，因为它削弱了整个技能/子代理投入的价值。

  5. #22745 — P2 EPIC：AST 感知的文件读取、搜索和代码库映射（7 条评论，1 👍）。跟踪 AST 感知工具是否能减少错位读取、轮次数量和 token 噪声。配套 issue #22746（CLI 工具，tilth/glyph）和 #22747（ast-grep）表明这正被拆解为具体实验。

  6. #21983 — P1：浏览器子代理在 Wayland 上失败（4 条评论，1 👍）。在已经失败的情况下打印 “Browser Agent Finished / Termination Reason: GOAL”——与 #22323 相同的虚假成功模式，如今还带有 Linux 显示服务器维度。

  7. #24246 — P2：作用域内工具过多时出现 400 错误（3 条评论）。标题提到 >128 个工具，正文提到 >400 个；无论如何，代理没有对启用工具进行作用域划分的策略，因此大型 MCP 配置可能硬失败。

  8. #22672 — P2：代理应停止/劝阻破坏性行为（3 条评论，1 👍）。在存在更安全路径时，模型会动用 git reset/--force，并且对数据库等有状态资源缺乏护栏。这与无人值守/YOLO 使用直接相关。

  9. #22186 — P1：get-shit-done 输出钩子导致崩溃（3 条评论）。打印最终摘要时可复现崩溃——也就是说，失败发生在将结果交还给用户的时刻。

  10. #22598 — P3：子代理轨迹应可通过 /chat share 查看（2 条评论，1 👍）。轨迹已被记录但无法访问，阻碍了子代理审查和评估。小功能，却能极大帮助调试上述问题。

同样值得关注： #22267（浏览器代理忽略 settings.json 覆盖项，例如 maxTurns）、#20079（符号链接的代理 .md 文件未被发现）、#21924（无闪烁终端调整大小）、#18836（用基于文件的持久化任务 CRUD 替换 WriteToDo）。

4. 关键 PR 进展

  1. #29918 — feat(cli)：通过 OSC 7501 上报 working/blocked/idle 状态（XL）。发出 Program Status 报告，使终端能够呈现多个会话中哪一个需要关注。这是迈向多会话、终端原生代理工作流的有意义一步。

  2. #29919 — feat(cli)：--append-system-prompt（L）。新增 --append-system-prompt、--append-system-prompt-file 和 GEMINI_APPEND_SYSTEM_MD。填补了一个真实空白：目前 GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD 会替换整个提示词，因此要添加一行项目上下文就意味着得 fork 整个提示词。

  3. #20406 — perf(core)：大型工具输出的内存管理（XL）。将过大的 shell 输出写入磁盘而不是缓存在内存中，修复截断路径中的 V8 OOM。该 PR 推进时间长，且对大型仓库用户影响很大。

  4. #23917 — feat(ui)：StyleSpan 抽象（XL）。用游程编码替代逐字符 toStyledCharacters() 分配，针对复杂 TableRenderer 场景中 280MB+ 的堆膨胀。

  5. #29910 — fix(acp)：权限请求中的 MCP 元数据 + 客户端信任（M）。将服务器/工具名称填充到 toolCall._meta['gemini-cli'].mcp，并允许 ACP 客户端通过 _meta.trust 预授权客户端提供的 MCP 服务器——这对编辑器集成部署很重要。

  6. #29778 — fix(acp)：在发送给模型前截断工具输出（M）。truncateToolOutputThreshold 在 --acp 模式下从未生效，因此一次大型 shell 输出就可能以 400 错误突破输入限制。消除了一处显著的 ACP 与 CLI 行为差异。

  7. #29783 — P1 fix(core)：为 read_many_files 资源匹配 include 模式（M）。用真正的模式匹配替代子串检查；此前任何文本重叠都可能将用户从未请求的二进制资源内联。

  8. #29782 — P1 fix(core)：沙箱拒绝启发式中的退出码空值检查（S）。对于 null，exitCode !== undefined 始终为 true，因此每个退出码为 null 的结果都会进入拒绝分支。小改动，但与安全相关的正确性修复。

  9. #29912 — fix(core)：从 web_fetch URL 中去除尾部标点/不配对括号（M）。new URL() 会欣然接受尾随逗号，因此逗号分隔的 URL 列表会生成受污染的 URL 并导致下游失败。

  10. #29779 — fix(core)：将失败的 ripgrep 搜索标记为工具错误（M）。RipGrepTool 返回失败时未设置 error，因此调度器将其记录为成功，同时又告诉模型搜索失败——这是与 #22323 同类的静默事实偏差 bug。

另已合并/关闭或进行中： #29890（仅在成功恢复后恢复工作区目录）、#29746（PowerShell 替换引号跟踪）、#29785（在 EOS 时分发最终的 Code Assist SSE 事件）、#29902（文档：commandPrefix 匹配命令名称而非效果——建议为无人值守运行使用允许列表）。

5. 热门讨论

本时间窗未提供讨论数据，因此省略本节。

6. 功能请求趋势

  • 子代理编排与可观测性。 目前最大的集群：准确的终止语义（#22323）、/chat share 中的轨迹可见性（#22598）、通过 settings.json 发现（#18285）、共享内存/并行协作（#18287），以及代理对自身标志和快捷键的自我感知（#21432）。贯穿始终的主线是让多代理运行可检查且可信。
  • 上下文与 token 节俭。 AST 感知的读取/搜索/映射（#22745、#22746、#22747）和 “Tactful Extraction” 外科手术式读取层级（#19561）都针对每轮约 36.6k token 的基线，以及因不加筛选的文件读取而导致的每轮 +15k 膨胀。
  • 沙箱化优先于限制。 #19873 主张零依赖操作系统沙箱加上执行后意图路由，使模型能够安全地使用原生 bash 惯用法；#22672 要求为破坏性命令设置护栏；#18397 要求按工作区（而非全局）划分策略作用域。
  • 上下文之外的持久状态。 #18836 和 #21000 都将任务跟踪从提示词中推到文件系统（或原生文件工具）上，以避免上下文腐化和会话丢失。
  • 更智能的工具作用域划分。 #24246 要求代理推理哪些工具已启用，而不是盲目挂载所有工具并触发 400。
  • 将终端 UX 作为一等界面。 无闪烁调整大小（#21924）和 OSC 7501 状态上报（#29918）反映了用户正在运行许多并发 CLI 会话。

7. 开发者痛点

  • 虚假成功报告。 跟踪器中腐蚀性最强的单一模式：MAX_TURNS 以 GOAL 成功的形式出现（#22323）、Wayland 浏览器失败也报告 GOAL（#21983）、ripgrep 失败被记录为成功（#29779）。开发者无法信任退出信号，这破坏了自动化和评估。
  • 无超时或诊断信息的无限期挂起。 通用代理委派（#21409）和 vite create 等交互式提示（#22465）会一直停滞，直到手动取消；用户报告等待一小时。唯一已知的修复方法是禁用该功能。
  • 被静默忽略的配置。 浏览器代理跳过 settings.json 中诸如 maxTurns 的覆盖项（#22267），符号链接的代理文件未被发现（#20079），并且 truncateToolOutputThreshold 在 ACP 模式下不起作用（#29778）。配置面与配置行为出现分歧。
  • 转义和引号边界情况。 错误的 \n 处理（#22466）、PowerShell 替换引号失步（#29746）和 URL 分词（#29912）都源于围绕 shell 和文本边界的简单字符串处理。
  • 平台特定故障。 Wayland（#21983）、泰语/老挝语 SARA AM 宽度（nightly 修复）和 Windows 引号处理继续产生各自的问题流——跨平台一致性是一项持续成本。
  • 内存与渲染开销。 大型工具输出导致 OOM（#20406）、表格渲染中的逐字符分配（#23917）以及调整大小闪烁（#21924）都指向 TUI 的扩展极限。
  • 工作区卫生与影响范围。 散落在各个目录中的临时脚本（#23571）和破坏性 git 操作（#22672）使无人值守运行难以清理且难以信任。
  • 提示词层的可扩展性缺口。 缺少非破坏性的系统提示词追加（由 #29919 解决），迫使用户为了一行项目指令而替换整个提示词。

过去 24 小时内没有 Pull Request 更新（总计：0 项）。 本摘要窗口内没有可报告的合并或审查活动。

已省略——未提供 Discussions 数据。

根据本窗口内更新的 20 个 issue 提炼：

  • 替代交互界面 — 本地 Web UI/基于浏览器的 agent（#3301，👍3）是获赞最多的请求；同一类还有：为改善长时间会话使用体验将输入框固定到屏幕顶部（#5227）。
  • ACP / 非交互模式与 TUI 的对等性 — Computer Use 插件在 CLI 中已启用，但在 ACP 模式下不可用（#5049）；捆绑插件和 MCP 功能的门控在无头路径与交互路径之间不一致。

  • 插件/技能命名空间一致性 — #5249 要求面向模型的 skill() 工具与斜杠命令已使用的 /plugin:skill 约定保持一致。
  • 服务器模式韧性 — #5242 请求 MCP 配置监视失败时优雅降级（重试/退避/watch 预算），而不是放弃会话队列。

  • 回归问题与功能迭代速度相伴。 #5243（exit_plan_mode 后子代理工具丢失，1.0.95 之后）和 #5228（新 Sessions 浏览器导致 --resume 损坏）是新交付的功能面在悄然回归——用户要求围绕计划批准和会话选择增加回归测试。
  • 长时间运行的 agent 无法维持上下文。 #5205（轮转时缺少 checkpoint.md）连同 #1616 和 #5243 表明，长时间自主运行——Autopilot 的标志性用例——仍然缺乏可靠的完成路径。
  • 成本可预测性是信任问题。 Assisted Permissions 配额事件（#4802）量小但严重性高：模糊的计费结果比功能缺口更快侵蚀采用率，用户希望有文档化的归因路径。
  • 静默、低信号的失败模式。 #5249（Skill not found）、#5243（工具静默缺失）和 #5107（在覆盖 HOME 时对无害 echo 触发 script_action_changed）都会在缺乏可操作诊断信息的情况下失败——这是对更清晰错误呈现的一再请求。

OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode 社区摘要 — 2026-10-25

今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有新版本发布，社区注意力几乎完全被一个广泛存在的 免费层配额故障 占据：v1 和 v2、CLI 和 Desktop 用户均报告在零使用量情况下出现 “Free usage exceeded” 错误，86,400 秒冷却时间会归零后反复循环，而不是正常重置。与此同时，维护者合并了一大批核心可靠性 PR，涵盖会话完整性、子代理结果上报、优雅关闭以及目录/ETag 优化。

发布

过去 24 小时内未发布新版本。

热门 Issue

  1. [#58831] 免费配额超时永远无法恢复，在 86400s 处呈锯齿状波动 — link 当前配额 bug 最清晰的复现：倒计时归零后立即重置为 86,400s。这是影响所有免费用户的权益重置故障的标志性讨论帖。

  2. [#58830] v1 和 v2 的免费使用限额连续两天未重置 — link 证实该回归同时波及 两个 大版本，排除了仅限 v2 的迁移问题。在一次成功请求后，所有免费模型都失败——这强烈表明按账户的使用计数器被错误持久化或读取。

  3. [#58828] “OpenCode 真的坏了，必须立刻修复” — link 一条情绪激烈的升级投诉，报告 Go 和 Zen 模型立即出现配额耗尽，即使没有订阅的用户也要等待 86,400s。说明该配额 bug 正在导致用户流失和敌意反馈。

  4. [#58781] OpenCode Desktop 1.19.4 中所有免费模型均显示 Free Usage Exceeded — link 本时段内获赞最多的 issue（👍 5）。Desktop 特定视角加上票数，使其成为反映免费层更广泛用户情绪的最佳风向标。

  5. [#58605] 闲置一周后出现 “Free usage exceeded”（Desktop） — link 补充了一个关键细节：重试计时器显示 “retrying in 72970s - attempt no. 1”，这表明剩余配额或过期时间戳格式异常，而不是真实的使用计数。

  6. [#58827] 尚未提交任何提示词就触发了使用限制 — link 零提示词即耗尽是最有力证据，说明检查在发出任何请求 之前 就已失败——即权益/认证查找失败，而非过度消耗。

  7. [#58724] 手动压缩遗漏必需的 recent，永久损坏会话 — link 严重的数据完整性 bug：schema 解码拒绝已持久化的压缩消息，导致后续每次读取都失败，fork 出的会话也被污染——且应用内无法恢复。对长时间运行的会话影响很大。

  8. [#58527] 权限 “ask” 静默允许 edit/write — link 一个与安全相关的 bug：ask 对 shell 会渲染审批对话框，但对 edit/write 却表现得像 allow。一个承诺显式同意的工具却静默写入文件，这会破坏信任。

  9. [#52925] opencode api get 在管道输出时截断 stdout — link 在较大（约 580 KB）响应下破坏了标准的 opencode api get ... | jq 工作流，而文件重定向正常。自 Oct 3 以来长期存在且仍未关闭——是脚本/CI 的阻塞问题。

  10. [#58533] Desktop 自定义提供商对话框写入 V1 密钥，V2 服务器忽略 — link 代表了 v1→v2 迁移类故障：以旧格式写入的配置会产生令人困惑的 “provider not available on this server” toast 提示。值得与 #58529（DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free 无限循环）和 #57931（过期的免费模型阻塞整个目录）一起强调，它们都具有“一个坏模型污染整个目录”的模式。

其他值得关注： #55077 — GPT-6.1 Sol 上下文窗口在 v2.0.28 中提升到 628k，但仍未达到宣传的 1.05M；#58558 — 硬编码的 1s 发现超时会让远程 Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM 端点静默返回零模型（已关闭）；#58559 — Windows %temp% 重定位会导致 CLI 崩溃（已关闭）。

关键 PR 进展

  1. [#58820] perf(core): 在 worker 中调整图像尺寸，空闲时释放 photon 内存 — link 通过将图像大小调整移出主线程并在 10s 后让 worker 空闲，消除了每张大图导致的 420–460 ms 服务器冻结，并回收约 250 MB 保留的 WASM 内存。显著提升 Desktop/web 响应性。

  2. [#58817] fix(cli): 用 10s 截止时间限制服务器关闭 — link 此前在 SIGTERM/SIGINT 后，清理过程可能永远挂起，且不提示卡在哪一步。现在会记录待处理工作并以状态码 1 退出，同时处理第二次信号。

  3. [#58825] fix(core): 将后台子代理后续轮次上报给其父级 — link 修复了当子代理进入空闲、随后被插件或合成消息唤醒时，父级收到 “Subagent completed without a text response” 的问题——这是面向多代理编排的正确性修复。

  4. [#58811] fix(schema): 以线性时间校验 base64 附件 — link 替换了一个容易发生灾难性回溯的正则表达式，该正则会在 每次 已存储消息解码时运行（历史重载、收件箱两次、投影器、GET messages）。显著改善延迟并增强健壮性。

  5. [#58813] fix(core): 使用 ETag 重新校验 models.dev 目录 — link 5 分钟刷新从未发送 If-None-Match，导致每个周期都重新下载并解析完整的约 6 MB 原始（约 413 KB brotli）目录，即使有可用的 304。

  6. [#55146] fix(core): 前台压缩使用会话传输 — link 前台摘要压缩即使在所选模型使用 WebSocket 时也通过 HTTP 发送。与 #58724 中出现的压缩相关故障直接相关。

  7. [#58790] fix(ai): 添加 compatibility.omitEmptyTools 以丢弃空 tools 数组 — link 解决某些提供商拒绝“有效工具集为空但历史记录包含工具调用/结果”的请求的问题——这是常见的跨提供商互操作故障。

  8. [#58788] fix(core): 当 patch 移动模拟重命名时保留文件模式 — link “Move to” 实现为先写入再删除，会静默丢失目标位置的权限。对于代理操作到的脚本和可执行文件很重要。

  9. [#58800] perf(core): 无变化时跳过集成列表重建 — link 每个会话步骤都会多次重建集成列表，每次遍历都解码所有已存储的凭据。缓存修复显著降低了每步开销。

  10. [#58310] fix(cli): 跨卷保留 Windows 二进制文件 — link 当包和缓存位于不同的 Windows 卷时，保留操作会因 EXDEV 失败；这与 #58559 中的 %temp% 重定位崩溃互为补充。

其他已合并/关闭： #58815（停止将服务 XDG_STATE_HOME 泄漏到工具 shell，命名端口所有者）、#58758（用 Decision 替换实验性评估）、#58771/#58770（针对 Google Interactions 和 AWS restJson1 的错误分类），以及文档更新 #58791（MiMo Code 移入已验证客户端）和 #58823（Luminary 记忆插件）。

功能请求趋势

  • 主题/自定义可扩展性 — #58824 请求为内置主题（Catppuccin Mocha、Tokyo Night）提供主题覆盖和语言 token 扩展，而不是固定的作用域映射。用户希望在不 fork 主题的情况下扩展主题。
  • 更好的多代理可观测性 — #58809 请求在 Desktop v2 的运行中子代理列表中显示每个子代理的 实际生效 模型和推理强度。随着子代理编排增长，了解子代理实际在做什么的可见性需求也在增长。
  • 更严格的轮次控制/引导语义 — #58776 提出带预期轮次保护的条件式引导准入，只有当会话仍拥有该轮次时才接纳纠正。
  • 面向工具调用模型的 Schema 清晰度 — #55504 指出 sessionID 在 TypeScript 中是可选的，但序列化后会让模型将其视为必需，推动生成更明确的 JSON Schema。

开发者痛点

  1. 免费层权益检查是主要故障模式。 本时段至少有十几个 issue（#58536、#58550、#58553、#58557、#58605、#58781、#58827、#58828、#58829、#58830、#58831、#58832）报告在零次或一次请求后就出现配额耗尽。报告覆盖 CLI v2.1.1、Desktop 1.19.4 和 v2，以及多个地区/IP——指向服务器端计数器或权益查找问题，而非客户端过度使用。不重置的 86,400s 计时器和 “retrying in 72970s” 表明时间戳处理也已损坏。

  2. v1 → v2 迁移仍然粗糙。 以 V1 格式（provider、npm、options）写入的配置会被 V2 服务器静默忽略（#58533），而专门为避开 v1 配额 bug 而迁移的用户，会在全新密钥上遇到 API 密钥过期（#58832）。

  3. 版本/配置漂移导致脆弱行为。 硬编码的 1 秒发现超时（#58558）、过期免费模型使整个目录失效（#57931），以及过时的模型元数据（#55077），都表明需要优雅降级，而不是全有或全无的失败。

  4. 数据完整性和同意保证正受到质疑。 手动压缩可能永久损坏会话（#58724），而 ask 权限会静默允许文件写入（#58527）。两者都在侵蚀人们对长时间运行代理工作流的信心。

  5. Windows 和 shell 边界情况仍然存在。 %temp% 重定位会导致 CLI 崩溃（#58559），跨卷二进制保留会因 EXDEV 失败（#58310），而 Nushell PATH 设置直到最近才得到支持（#51227）。

  6. 脚本化能力缺口。 opencode api get 截断管道输出（#52925）会阻塞标准的 | jq 和 CI 自动化模式——一个小修复对工具用户影响巨大。

本时段未提供讨论数据，因此省略“热门讨论”部分。

  • Provider 广度与正确路由。 按数量看最主要的主题：新的按量付费 provider（#11369）、托管推理端点（#11370）、Vertex 上的 Claude（#11371）、Bedrock 的 Mantle 路由（#11372），以及感知 effort 的模型预设（#11355）。方向是声明式的逐 provider 目录，而不是生成列表。

  • 面向真实产品的扩展 API 接口面。 用于宿主自有存储的 Code Mode 输出写入器（#11070）、watchEvents 从最后可见条目恢复（#11327）、确定性的 provider 默认值（#8810），以及支持 span 参数、summary-model 覆盖和 entry 引用的可组合压缩（#11310）。

7. 开发者痛点

  • 流式性能是长会话的首要阻塞项。 参与度最高的三个 issue 中有两个（#6665、#7730）描述了流式输出时占满一个完整核心，根因追溯到每块重建 Markdown、未缓存字素分割，以及（此前的 #9265）二次方级工具参数重复解析。嵌入式宿主感受最深，因为事件循环被阻塞会拖住每一个共同托管的会话。
  • Provider 集成会在边缘场景的传输和负载形状上出问题。 无错误但停滞的流（#4945）、跨 chunk 拆分的 CRLF（#10390）、丢失的 thought signatures（#10157）、被拒绝的嵌套图片（#8643）和过期的 AWS 凭证（#11221），都是“一直能用直到突然不能用”的失败，会在轮次中途暴露，且很难从 TUI 诊断。
  • 扩展生态脆弱性。 注册 provider、在 session_start 发送消息或会话中途重载的扩展，可能静默改变核心行为——丢失 Anthropic system 字段（#11157）、用 tool_reference_unresolved 破坏所有后续请求（#11376），或把会话切到错误的默认模型（#8810）。
  • 终端兼容性回归反复出现。 1.3.0 的发布带来一波 UI 卫生 bug：Ctrl+Shift+C 丢失提示词（#11379）、CSI 鼠标/焦点负载泄漏到 PowerShell（#11205）、stripAnsi 残留 private-parameter 序列（#11377），以及 Alacritty IME 自动补全失败（#11177）。
  • 分诊吞吐量与贡献者意图。 若干未采取行动即关闭的 issue（#9265、#10642、#11310、#10145、#8642）附带了原型、补丁或生产影响，且 #8643 明确指出此前的 PR 被贡献门禁自动关闭。再加上许多 untriaged 条目在提交当天就被关闭，感知到的评审门槛成为反复出现的摩擦来源。

  • 延期评审债务。 一种反复出现的模式：承载非阻塞评审建议的“后续”issue（#14973、#13698、#14625、#12986）表明评审吞吐量超过了合并与清理能力。

item.content:encoded:
AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-10-25

Generated: 2026-10-25 00:29 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code
  • Claude Code Skills

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool Comparison: AI CLI Developer Tools — 2026-10-25

1. Ecosystem Overview

The 2026-10-25 digests show a market shifting from capability demos to operational trust. Claude Code is in a visible maintenance trough with high-consensus plan-tier demand and unresolved sandbox data-loss reports, while Codex is concentrated on Windows/app-server stability and MCP resource isolation. Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Copilot CLI, and Qwen Code are all iterating on agent orchestration, resource lifecycle, quota/auth correctness, and platform parity. Across communities, the central question is no longer “can the agent code?” but “can it finish reliably, recover safely, and report truthfully?” Enterprise buying signals—Claude Team 20x, Copilot billing incidents, Qwen CI/runtime automation—are increasingly prominent.

2. Activity Comparison

Counts below are digest-reported within the 24h window, not full repository totals. “Notable/listed” means items explicitly profiled in the digest. n/d = no count provided in the digest. N/A would be used only for disabled community channels; none of these seven tools had Issues/PRs disabled upstream in this dataset.

Tool Issues count PR count Discussions count Release status
Claude Code 50 updated; 10 profiled 2 updated; 0 merged n/d No release
OpenAI Codex 10 notable; total n/r 0 updated 10 profiled (8 show-and-tell, 2 Q&A) No release
Gemini CLI 14 notable (10 hot + 4 watch) 14 listed (10 key + 4 other) n/d 1 nightly (v0.67.0-nightly.20261024)
GitHub Copilot CLI 20 updated 0 updated n/d 2 patches (v1.0.104-2, v1.0.104-3)
OpenCode 13 notable; ≥12 quota reports cited (overlap) 16 listed (10 key + 6 other) n/d No release
Pi 12 notable 10 listed 2 profiled No release
Qwen Code 13 notable 15 listed (10 key + 5 other) n/d 2 releases (v0.26.1, desktop-v0.26.1)

Reading the table: Claude has the broadest issue window and strongest single-issue engagement, but zero merged PR activity. Gemini, Qwen, OpenCode, and Pi show denser code-review throughput. Codex and Copilot’s “0 PR updated” figures are snapshot limitations or low PR visibility, not proof that no work is happening.

3. Shared Feature Directions

Seven cross-tool requirements recur across multiple communities:

  1. Truthful agent state and termination semantics

    • Gemini: false GOAL success on MAX_TURNS and browser failures (#22323, #21983, #29779).
    • Codex: evidence-backed completion reports (#36718).
    • Copilot: silent subagent tool loss and broken context rollover (#5243, #5205).
    • OpenCode: parent agents not receiving later subagent turns (#58825).
    • Qwen: fallback chains skipped by misclassified 429s (#13895).
    • Need: explicit success/failure reasons, evidence mapping, parent-child result propagation, and auditable completion claims.

  2. Background/parallel task lifecycle and resource isolation

    • Copilot: background shell completion corrupting turns (#4946), inotify exhaustion (#5242), context rollover failure (#5205).
    • Codex: per-thread MCP process explosion (#53285), git diff fan-out (#43019), ephemeral threads leaking MCP stacks (#39783).
    • OpenCode: bounded shutdown (#58817), background subagent reporting (#58825).
    • Pi: full-core TUI pinning during streaming (#6665, #7730).
    • Need: bounded process concurrency, cleanup/reclamation, timeouts, backpressure, and graceful shutdown.

  3. Quota, billing, and auth consistency

    • Claude: Team plan needs Max-20x-equivalent tier (#47509).
    • Codex: usage-limit resets not recognized across clients (#51043).
    • Copilot: Assisted Permissions PRU drain incident (#4802).
    • OpenCode: free-tier quota never resets; 86,400s loop (#58830, #58831, #58827).
    • Qwen: reasoning tokens double-counted in cost display (#15444).
    • Pi: usage-limit interruption/resume workflow (#11306).
    • Need: predictable entitlement state, cross-client syncing, accurate token accounting, and transparent reset semantics.

  4. Permission/sandbox trust and consent

    • Claude: destructive sandbox filesystem operations (#93287, #93408) and inconsistent auto-mode classifier (#101327).
    • Gemini: sandboxing over restriction (#19873), destructive-command guardrails (#22672).
    • OpenCode: permission “ask” silently allows edit/write (#58527).
    • Copilot: ACP OAuth refresh vs browser redirect (#5229).
    • Codex: opaque sandbox/permission states.
    • Need: deterministic approvals, legible sandbox boundaries, re-consent for tool expansion, safe defaults, and dry-run/recovery paths.

  5. Provider/model routing and interoperability

    • Pi: large provider-expansion PR chain (#11368–#11372), Gemini thought signatures (#10157), Bedrock image payloads (#8643).
    • OpenCode: v1→v2 config mismatch (#58533), catalog poisoning by expired models (#57931).
    • Qwen: strict OpenAI-compatible tool schemas (#12222), 429 fallback classification (#13895).
    • Gemini: too many tools in scope causing 400s (#24246).
    • Codex: model-routing opacity and silent model switches.
    • Need: declarative model catalogs, capability-aware routing, graceful fallbacks, and adapter-level conformance tests.

  6. Context, memory continuity, and compaction

    • OpenCode: manual compaction can permanently brick a session (#58724).
    • Qwen: transcript snapshot index cap makes sessions unopenable (#13113).
    • Codex: AGENTS.md propagation checks and decision maps across fresh chats.
    • Pi: extension ordering loses Anthropic system field (#11157), embedded-session memory retention (#10642).
    • Gemini: persistent file-based task state (#18836).
    • Need: durable session stores, recoverable compaction, context handoff, and memory isolation across projects.

  7. Terminal/Desktop/headless parity

    • Claude: Desktop prompt suggestions, plugin render hooks, Remote Control persistence.
    • Codex: Windows VS Code startup, iPad remote sessions, Windows MCP process counts.
    • Gemini: Wayland browser subagent failures, OSC 7501 terminal status.
    • Copilot: Windows proxy/STT, ACP parity, local web UI request.
    • OpenCode: Windows %temp% relocation, cross-volume binary retention.
    • Pi: Ctrl+Shift+C prompt loss, Windows CSI leakage, Alacritty IME.
    • Qwen: Web Shell i18n fallback blocking non-English browsers.
    • Need: cross-platform CI matrices, headless parity, accessible UI fallbacks, and terminal-native status reporting.

4. Differentiation Analysis

Tool Feature focus Target users Technical approach
Claude Code Team plan tiering, Desktop/TUI polish, sandbox safety, plugin rendering, Remote Control Teams, enterprise procurement, power users Sandboxed Bash/Desktop, permission classifier, plugin UI hooks, Remote Control, Max-tier usage model
OpenAI Codex Windows desktop/app-server stability, IDE extension, MCP lifecycle, remote/mobile, AGENTS.md Windows/IDE developers, ChatGPT-authenticated users, enterprise app users App-server + VS Code extension, MCP, thread/history APIs, evidence-backed completion direction
Gemini CLI Subagent reliability, ACP/editor integration, terminal-native status, AST-aware context, sandboxing Terminal/editor developers in Google ecosystem CLI + ACP, subagent orchestration, OSC 7501, AST/tool-scoping experiments, zero-dependency sandbox proposals
GitHub Copilot CLI Autopilot async correctness, SDK/ACP/headless, plugin skills, enterprise proxy/OAuth GitHub enterprise, CI/container users, Copilot subscribers Autopilot, MCP, ACP, plugin namespacing, managed model fusion, patch-release cadence
OpenCode Free-tier/Desktop, v2 migration, provider interop, session integrity Individual developers, free-tier users, Desktop/CLI users Client/server session transport, model catalog ETag, subagents, themes, desktop/CLI convergence
Pi Provider breadth, extension API, TUI performance, embedded SDK, long sessions Power users, extension authors, embedded/multi-session hosts Declarative provider definitions, models.dev catalog, TUI performance work, extension lifecycle APIs
Qwen Code CI/PR automation, runtime broker/Kubernetes, Desktop/daemon, cost accounting Qwen ecosystem, self-hosted/enterprise CI teams CLI + daemon/Desktop, runtime broker, managed agent, strict OpenAI-compatible provider handling

The strategic split is between platform-owned enterprise stacks—Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI—and ecosystem/extensibility-led tools—OpenCode, Pi, and Qwen Code. The former compete on integration depth, admin controls, and safety; the latter compete on provider coverage, customization, and rapid iteration.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

  • Highest raw engagement: Claude Code and Pi. Claude’s #47509 reached 187 👍 / 67 comments, and its sandbox data-loss cluster is safety-critical. Pi’s #4945 has 88 comments / 35 👍, signaling deep long-session reliability pain.
  • Strong issue-intake activity: Copilot CLI (20 issues updated), Claude (50-issue window), OpenCode (quota crisis with ≥12 reports), and Codex (Windows/app-server cluster). These communities are actively filing, but not all are seeing proportional merge throughput.
  • Fastest visible iteration: Gemini CLI (nightly + 14 listed PRs), Qwen Code (2 releases + 15 listed PRs), OpenCode (16 listed PRs), and Pi (stacked provider-expansion PR chain). These tools show maintainers actively landing correctness, performance, and provider work.
  • Maturity vs. velocity: Claude, Codex, Copilot, and Gemini have broader surfaces and enterprise adoption, but carry platform debt—sandbox trust, Windows stability, headless parity, stale triage. OpenCode, Pi, and Qwen are younger and more visibly iterating, but their process maturity lags: OpenCode’s entitlement incident and Pi’s contribution-gate closures show operational gaps.
  • Bottom line: Claude has the most consequential community signal but a stalled integration posture. Gemini, Qwen, OpenCode, and Pi are the most rapidly iterating. Codex and Copilot remain mature but constrained by Windows/headless reliability and low visible PR throughput in this snapshot.

6. Trend Signals

  1. Reliability is the new differentiation. False success reports, indefinite hangs, broken rollover, and background-task corruption appear across Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode, and Pi. Buyers should evaluate termination semantics, recovery paths, and evidence reporting—not just model quality.
  2. Resource isolation is moving up-stack. MCP per-thread processes, git diff fan-out, inotify exhaustion, and TUI CPU/RAM growth show that process budgets, backpressure, and cleanup are now core agent-runtime requirements.
  3. Billing/auth/quota transparency is a trust layer. Quota resets, PRU drain, token double-counting, and plan-tier ceilings are adoption blockers. Enterprises should demand auditable usage attribution and cross-client state consistency.
  4. Consent and sandbox legibility matter more than sandbox claims. Destructive filesystem operations, silent edit/write permissions, and nondeterministic classifiers erode trust. Explicit approval models, re-consent, dry-run, and filesystem boundaries are becoming table stakes.
  5. Provider-neutral adapters and fallbacks are strategic. Pi’s provider expansion, OpenCode’s v1→v2 migration pain, Qwen’s OpenAI-compatible strictness, and Gemini’s tool-scoping limits all point to declarative catalogs, capability routing, and conformance testing.
  6. Headless/CI/container parity will be a buying criterion. ACP, OAuth refresh, proxy awareness, inotify limits, Windows behavior, and non-English UI fallbacks are no longer edge cases—they determine whether tools work in enterprise CI and remote environments.
  7. Agent observability and eval tooling is emerging. Evidence-backed completion, AGENTS.md verification, subagent trajectory visibility, and pytest-based behavior checks are early signals of a new tooling layer around agent trust.
  8. Community operations are a leading indicator. Stale-bot closures, CI capacity bottlenecks, contribution gates, and release automation quality correlate directly with how quickly substantive issues get resolved. For decision-makers, PR throughput and triage health are practical support-quality signals.

Per-Tool Reports

Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code

Claude Code Skills Highlights

Source: anthropics/skills

Claude Code Skills — Community Highlights Report

Source: github.com/anthropics/skills · Data as of: 2026-10-25

Data caveat: Every PR in the supplied dataset reports Comments: undefined and 👍: 0, so ranking below uses attention proxies — number of PRs touching the same skill, linked Issues with high comment counts, and sustained update activity — rather than raw comment counts. All listed PRs are OPEN; no merged PRs appear in this snapshot.

1. Top Skills Ranking

# Skill Representative PR(s) Status Attention signal
1 skill-creator (meta-skill) #1298, #1681, #1997 Open 3 concurrent PRs + Issues #202 (8 comments), #1394 (4 comments)
2 mcp-builder #1742 Open Fixes #1668; chained to Issue #1390 (0/N eval scores)
3 webapp-testing #1980, #1976 Open 2 PRs, one security-grade (CWE-78)
4 docx #1792, #1734 Open 2 PRs + Issue #2018 (invalid XML output)
5 claude-api #1730 Open Linked to Issue #1487 (~156k token eager injection)
6 pyxel (retro game dev) #525 Open (draft-stage) Longest-running active feature PR — Mar 5 → Oct 23
7 document-typography #514 Open Widow/orphan control for generated docs
8 skill-quality-analyzer / skill-security-analyzer #83 Open Oldest open PR in set (2025-11-06)

Detail notes

  • skill-creator is the ecosystem's pressure point: three open fixes address trigger-eval false misses and Windows subprocess handling (#1298), standalone package_skill.py execution (#1681, most recently updated 2026-10-24), and hand-rolled YAML frontmatter parsing that corrupts descriptions (#1997). Issue #202 argues the skill reads like developer documentation rather than an operational instruction set.
  • mcp-builder #1742 adapts to mcp>=2.0.0, where streamablehttp_client was renamed and custom headers now route through create_mcp_http_client. Paired with Issue #1390 (evaluation harness fabricates tool errors), this skill's testing path is the community's main complaint.
  • webapp-testing carries the clearest security framing: #1980 removes shell=True from with_server.py to close a command-injection vector; #1976 corrects textarea/select misreporting in element discovery.
  • pyxel #525 and document-typography #514 are the strongest net-new skill proposals: headless frame inspection for retro games, and typographic QC (orphan wrap, widow paragraphs, numbering alignment) for generated documents.

2. Community Demand Trends

Distilled from Issues, demand clusters into five directions — notably, most are about trust and reliability rather than new capabilities:

  1. Namespace integrity & supply-chain trust — Issue #492 (46 comments, the most-discussed issue in the dataset) warns that community skills shipping under the anthropic/ namespace enable impersonation and permission escalation. Reinforced by the eval-viewer XSS report (#1394).
  2. Team/org-level skill distribution — #228 (17 comments) asks for org-wide skill libraries and share links instead of manual .skill file passing; #189 reports duplicate content across document-skills and example-skills plugins.
  3. Reliable skill triggering & evaluation — #556 (13 comments): run_eval.py yields a 0% trigger rate across all queries, meaning skill authors cannot validate their work.
  4. Context/token economy — #1487: claude-api eagerly injects ~156k tokens in a single tool call; #202: skill-creator prose is too verbose for token efficiency.
  5. Meta-skills for quality & governance — proposals for a three-gate reasoning pipeline (#1385), agent-governance safety patterns (#412), and symbolic compact-memory notation (#1329).

3. High-Potential Pending Skills

PRs with recent activity and narrow, reviewable diffs — candidate near-term landings:

PR Skill Why it's likely to land
#1681 skill-creator Updated 2026-10-24 (freshest in set); fixes a reproducible ModuleNotFoundError
#1980 webapp-testing Security fix (CWE-78) with a self-contained change surface
#1997 skill-creator Correct YAML scalar parsing; replaces a manual parser
#1977 algorithmic-art One-function fix (wrapAround() modulo), resolves #1897
#1976 webapp-testing Tag-name reporting fix, resolves #1891
#1792 docx LibreOffice timeout now reported as error + output verification
#1730 claude-api Dead-URL replacement, HTTP-200 verified

Longer-horizon but high-value: #1742 (mcp-builder, MCP v2 compat) and #538 (pdf, case-sensitive reference fixes).

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's most concentrated demand is not for new Skills but for the trust, correctness, and measurability of the skill toolchain itself — namespace integrity, reliable triggering/evaluation, and token-efficient skill-creator/mcp-builder plumbing dominate discussion, while net-new skills (pyxel, ODT, document-typography, md2video-audio) remain a secondary, slower-moving stream.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-10-25

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases shipped in the last 24 hours, and the PR queue is effectively dormant (2 closed PRs, 0 merges to highlight). Community attention remains concentrated on plan tiering — issue #47509 crossed 187 👍 and 67 comments demanding a Max-20x-equivalent Team seat — and on a pair of data-loss incident reports (#93287, #93408) where sandboxed Bash/Desktop sessions allegedly deleted macOS Applications and home-directory contents. Meanwhile the Desktop Code tab continues to accumulate small but high-friction regressions around prompt suggestions, plugin render hooks, and Remote Control session persistence.

2. Releases

Omitted — no releases published in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #47509 — Team plan needs a Max 20x equivalent tier (OPEN, 67 comments, 187 👍) The single most-engaged item in the window. Teams standardize on Claude Code for agentic workflows but hit the 6.25x Premium ceiling while individuals run Max 20x. Signals real enterprise procurement friction — the 👍 count is ~3x anything else here.

  2. #93287 — Claude Code deleted entire macOS Applications directory (OPEN, high-priority, data-loss, sandbox) Alleges every installed app was removed. Tone is raw, but the metadata (high-priority + data-loss + area:sandbox) is the alarming part. This is the flagship of a cluster of sandbox-escalation reports.

  3. #93408 — Desktop deleted macOS home folder contents including keychain (OPEN, high-priority, data-loss) Companion report to #93287, implicating Bash + Desktop sandbox boundaries. Keychain loss elevates this from annoyance to security incident; both remain open after ~6 weeks.

  4. #103335 — Desktop prompt suggestions (Tab to accept) stopped appearing (OPEN, has repro, 11 comments) Regressed around the 2026-10-13 update and survives restarts and fresh sessions. A quiet productivity loss for heavy Desktop users; reproducible, which usually shortens time-to-fix.

  5. #102988 — Style sidebar session rows by state (OPEN, enhancement, 7 comments) Requests full-row color encoding (running / needs-input / unread / cache-expired) instead of a single status dot. Well-specified; reflects how crowded parallel-agent sessions have become.

  6. #101327 — Auto-mode permission classifier blocks routine pre-approved writes (OPEN, area:permissions) Classifier categories shift between runs and block even self-service permission edits. The inconsistency — not the blocking itself — is the complaint; it makes auto-mode untrustworthy for scripted workflows.

  7. #102480 — Next-step box hides plugin AbovePrompt render (OPEN, has repro, Windows) A Desktop UI layering bug that breaks the documented plugin extension point. Small blast radius today, but it undermines confidence in the modding API's rendering contract.

  8. #83528 — No way to clear the prompt buffer without a side effect (OPEN, area:tui) Careful audit showing every existing keybinding either partially clears or arms /clear destructively. Classic TUI papercut amplified by long multi-line agentic prompts.

  9. #103959 — Plugin pane can't be widened past 45% of terminal (OPEN, Linux, 3 👍) Regression on the docked-plugin layout, first reported 2026-10-21. Narrow but zero-comment-resistance — users agree it's a regression, not a design choice.

  10. #104700 — Remote Control sessions go offline until touched locally (OPEN, duplicate, Windows) Sessions drop off Remote Control after sleep/resume even with the machine awake. Marked duplicate, which suggests it's a known family of state-persistence bugs rather than an isolated case.

4. Key PR Progress

Only 2 pull requests were updated in the window, both CLOSED and neither merged — treat this as a stalled-integration signal rather than feature progress.

  1. #62597 — fix: resolve 10 bugs across scripts and workflows (CLOSED) Hardens repo automation: replaces a hardcoded REPO with a GITHUB_REPOSITORY env fallback so scripts work in forks, adds safe fallbacks for github.event.repository.name on schedule/workflow_dispatch where it can be null, and improves error handling in edit-issue-labels.sh. Open since May — its closure without merge is notable given how much of the triage load (see the stale-close pattern below) depends on this tooling.

  2. #16132 — fix: /install-github-app support for dev container (CLOSED) Fixes a real onboarding blocker: after authenticating gh inside a dev container, /install-github-app still reported gh as unauthenticated. Resolved by adding the GitHub CLI repository to fetch the latest gh. Open since January.

Analyst note: With zero open PRs and no releases, the community's issue backlog is growing faster than it's being drained — a pattern that shows up directly in Section 7.

5. Hot Discussions

Omitted — no Discussions data was provided in this dataset.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Power-user plan tiering (B2B). #47509 dominates. The ask is structural: per-seat multipliers don't map to how agentic coding actually burns tokens, and teams want a 20x-class seat with admin/billing controls.
  • Desktop Code tab as a first-class multi-agent console. A tight cluster of requests (#102988, #102031, #101312) targets sidebar information density: state-based row styling, human-readable project-folder group names, and exposing the text-selection menu as a ui.render component. Users are running many concurrent sessions and the UI hasn't caught up.
  • Plugin/mod API surface expansion. #101312 and #102480 both concern the ui.render extension points (AbovePrompt, selection menu). Modders are pushing the API into layout territory Anthropic hasn't formalized.
  • Terminal compatibility & capability negotiation. #99566 asks the kitty-graphics probe to trust the actual graphics query response rather than matching XTVERSION strings against kitty/ghostty. SwiftTerm-based terminals (Moo) are being excluded despite supporting Unicode placeholders.
  • TUI ergonomics. #83528 and #103959 are both small, precise requests for predictable keybindings and resizable panes — the unglamorous work that determines whether the CLI feels professional.
  • Opt-out from behavior experiments. #89735 (closed stale) requested a documented switch to disable silent cohort experiments; #89860 shows the downstream symptom, with users surprised by unsolicited model switches. This is a transparency ask, not a feature ask.
  • Remote/headless session reliability. #104700 and #97368 point at a shared theme: session state and notifications don't survive sleep/resume, undermining phone-side or unattended operation.
  • Sandbox/security consent surfaces. #89866 (closed stale) flagged that remote MCP servers can add outward-facing tools to an already-trusted connector with no re-consent — a security-model gap, not a bug.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Destructive filesystem operations in sandboxed sessions. #93287 and #93408 are the acute cases, but the underlying complaint is broader: the trust boundary between "sandbox" and "real home directory" is not legible to users, and post-incident recovery is undocumented. This is the highest-severity theme in the dataset.
  2. Permission classifier unpredictability. #101327 describes the same operation being allowed and blocked across runs under shifting categories. Non-determinism in the permission layer forces users back to manual approval, which defeats auto-mode's purpose.
  3. Multi-agent workflows abort on a single denial. #88216 (closed stale) captured it well: pressing Esc or Deny on one tool call kills the entire parallel run. For anyone using Workflow/parallel subagents, this makes permission prompts disproportionately expensive.
  4. Data-integrity regressions in the Desktop session store. #89497 (Windows MSIX repair wiped 97 of 100 conversations), #89873 ("No messages yet" despite intact .jsonl), and #89871 (lastActivityAt stamped for a turn that never happened) describe a store that disagrees with its own on-disk truth.
  5. Silent behavior changes via cohort experiments. Unannounced shifts in tool selection, file-editing method (e.g., sed/heredocs instead of Read/Edit/Write), and system prompts break user expectations and any prompts/evals pinned to prior behavior.
  6. Stale-bot closing of substantive reports. A large share of today's 50-issue window is [CLOSED] [stale] — including security (#89866), data-loss (#89497), and agent-correctness (#82821) issues. The repo's own automation PRs (#62597) sit unmerged, so triage tooling appears to be decaying alongside the backlog.
  7. Install/update path collisions. #84224 (closed, reproduced) documents the auto-updater installing into the PATH-resolved npm prefix and clobbering a different install when multiple Node prefixes exist — a common nvm + Homebrew setup. Version-independent, so it will recur.
  8. Model-routing opacity. #89876 (advisor picking a different model than documented) and #89860 ("another stupid switch to opus 4.8 that wasn't warranted") show users don't feel in control of which model executes their work, and dislike discovering it after the fact.
  9. Notification and connectivity flakiness on Desktop. #97368 (intermittent turn-complete notifications), #89719 and #83745 (Claude-in-Chrome permanently "not connected" after orphaned claude.exe processes accumulate and exhaust named pipes). The latter has a known workaround — kill stale processes — that shouldn't be necessary.

Bottom line for 2026-10-25: the repo is in a maintenance trough — no releases, no open PRs, and a backlog being trimmed by stale-closure rather than resolution. The two signals worth watching are the Team 20x tier request (commercial, high-consensus) and the sandbox data-loss reports (safety-critical, currently unresolved).

OpenAI Codex — openai/codex

OpenAI Codex Community Digest — 2026-10-25

1. Today’s Highlights

Activity was dominated by Windows desktop/app-server stability and resource-isolation issues: VS Code extension startup failures, MCP process proliferation, git diff fan-out, and long-chat memory growth. The most-discussed thread remains #50329 with 33 comments, while #51043 drew the strongest positive reaction with 14 👍. No new releases or PR updates landed in the last 24h; discussions show strong interest in AGENTS.md verification, background/parallel Codex runs, and cross-agent context handoff.

2. Hot Issues

  1. #50329 — Windows App read_thread returns only chatgpt-content-reference for completed ChatGPT replies
    33 comments, 6 👍. A high-impact data-retrieval regression: completed ChatGPT replies are not returning full content to the Windows app. Community is actively triangulating package/version evidence.

  2. #41695 — iPad App freezes constantly when accessing Remote Codex Sessions
    22 comments, 2 👍. Remote-session reliability on iPad remains a recurring pain point, especially for Pro 20x users relying on mobile access.

  3. #36718 — Add evidence-backed completion reports for agent tasks
    22 comments. Proposes a structured requirement-to-evidence mapping so “task complete” claims are auditable. This aligns with growing demand for agent trust and verification.

  4. #43019 — Windows unbounded git diff --no-index fan-out exhausts commit and crashes Windows
    18 comments. With ~4,771 untracked files, Codex Desktop can spawn one git diff per file and exhaust system commit. A serious workspace-scale stability issue.

  5. #56691 — Codex 26.1021.22027 fails to start UI in VS Code 1.143.1 on Windows
    16 comments, 5 👍. A fresh IDE-extension regression with clear reproduction details. High reaction suggests broad Windows VS Code impact.

  6. #49767 — Windows official Library transfer helper crashes on os.setxattr
    16 comments. Blocks metadata-preserving materialization for skills/library workflows. Windows compatibility gap in a core Codex workflow.

  7. #39783 — Desktop ephemeral thread summaries leak full MCP stacks via thread/unsubscribe
    13 comments, 3 👍. Ephemeral summary threads inherit and start the full MCP configuration even though summarization does not use MCP tools. Resource and exposure concern.

  8. #53285 — Windows: one stdio MCP process set per thread; 353 processes / ~9.6 GiB
    8 comments. A concrete resource-lifecycle failure: MCP process sets are created per thread and reclamation lags creation. Directly affects long-running app-server stability.

  9. #51043 — Usage-limit reset not recognized by Pi; OpenAI model usage still blocked
    7 comments, 14 👍. Highest positive reaction in the issue set. Auth/usage-reset state is not propagating consistently across clients.

  10. #54540 — Windows recurring “workspace routing discovery timed out” during goals and subagent workflows
    10 comments, 3 👍. Subagent and goal workflows are sensitive to routing discovery timeouts, pointing to app-server connectivity/orchestration instability.

3. Key PR Progress

No pull requests were updated in the last 24h (0 items). There are no PRs to summarize from this snapshot; this is a data-availability limitation, not an indication that no work is in progress.

4. Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #55421 — TAHU: can an agent send a harmless email without leaking staff notes?
    8 comments. A Python authorization-gateway prototype exploring approval boundaries and privacy-preserving agent actions. Seeking three developer trials.

  • #55086 — KiraBridge + ThreadDesk: connecting seven tools for controllable, voice-driven vibe coding
    4 comments. Focused on scoped access, budget limits, traceable results, and preserving project context across interruptions.

  • #56176 — Does a fresh Codex session receive AGENTS.md? A repeatable before/after check
    4 comments. Provides a practical marker-based method for verifying instruction-path propagation after AGENTS.md or Codex changes.

  • #56181 — pytest-codex: turn AGENTS.md rules into pytest checks, with offline replay

Gemini CLI — google-gemini/gemini-cli

Gemini CLI Community Digest — 2026-10-25

1. Today's Highlights

Agent reliability remains the dominant theme: the two highest-engagement open issues are a P1 where subagent MAX_TURNS termination is misreported as GOAL success (#22323, 13 comments) and the P1 generalist-agent hang (#21409, 8 👍). On the PR side, contributors are pushing terminal-integration polish (OSC 7501 status reporting), system-prompt extensibility, and a cluster of correctness fixes in ACP, read_many_files, and shell-sandbox heuristics. A single nightly shipped in the last 24h with CLI stream-cancellation and CJK display-width fixes.

2. Releases

v0.67.0-nightly.20261024.gcd1b45c2d — release notes

Nightly build only (no stable release in this window). Visible changes:

  • CLI: stop continuation stream processing and auto-nudge after request cancellation (#29868) — prevents the CLI from continuing to consume/emit after a user cancels.
  • CLI: correct Thai and Lao SARA AM display width (#29868-adjacent PR by @elberthc-byte) — a terminal-width rendering fix for Southeast Asian scripts.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #22323 — P1: Subagent MAX_TURNS recovery reported as GOAL success (13 comments, 2 👍). codebase_investigator returns status: "success" / Termination Reason: "GOAL" despite its own output admitting it hit the turn limit before analyzing anything. This is the most-commented issue of the day because it corrupts orchestration semantics: callers cannot distinguish "finished" from "gave up," making multi-agent pipelines unverifiable.

  2. #21409 — P1: Generalist agent hangs (8 comments, 8 👍 — highest reaction count in the set). Simple operations like folder creation hang indefinitely once work is delegated; users report waiting up to an hour. The workaround (instructing the model not to defer to subagents) effectively disables the feature, which explains the strong community signal.

  3. #19873 — P2: Zero-dependency OS sandboxing + post-execution intent routing (9 comments). Proposes letting Gemini lean on its native bash affinity (grep/sed/awk chains) while containing risk via sandboxing rather than restricting tools. Notable as the main architectural counter-proposal to the current tool-permission model.

  4. #21968 — P2: Gemini does not use skills and sub-agents enough (7 comments). Anecdotal but widely shared: skills with clear descriptions (e.g. gradle, git) are ignored unless explicitly invoked. Matters because it undermines the value of the whole skills/subagent investment.

  5. #22745 — P2 EPIC: AST-aware file reads, search, and codebase mapping (7 comments, 1 👍). Tracks whether AST-aware tools reduce misaligned reads, turn count, and token noise. Companion issues #22746 (CLI tooling, tilth/glyph) and #22747 (ast-grep) show this is being decomposed into concrete experiments.

  6. #21983 — P1: Browser subagent fails on Wayland (4 comments, 1 👍). Prints "Browser Agent Finished / Termination Reason: GOAL" while having failed — the same false-success pattern as #22323, now with a Linux display-server dimension.

  7. #24246 — P2: 400 error when too many tools are in scope (3 comments). Title cites >128 tools, body cites >400; either way, the agent has no strategy for scoping enabled tools, so large MCP setups can hard-fail.

  8. #22672 — P2: Agent should stop/discourage destructive behavior (3 comments, 1 👍). Model reaches for git reset/--force when safer paths exist, and lacks guardrails around stateful resources like databases. Directly relevant to unattended/YOLO usage.

  9. #22186 — P1: get-shit-done output hook causes crash (3 comments). Reproducible crash while printing the final summary — i.e. the failure lands at the moment of handing results back to the user.

  10. #22598 — P3: Subagent trajectory should be visible via /chat share (2 comments, 1 👍). Trajectories are recorded but not reachable, blocking subagent review and evals. Small feature, high leverage for debugging the issues above.

Also worth watching: #22267 (Browser Agent ignores settings.json overrides such as maxTurns), #20079 (symlinked agent .md files not discovered), #21924 (flicker-free terminal resize), #18836 (replace WriteToDo with persistent file-based task CRUD).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #29918 — feat(cli): report working/blocked/idle status via OSC 7501 (XL). Emits Program Status reports so terminals can surface which of several sessions needs attention. A meaningful step toward multi-session, terminal-native agent workflows.

  2. #29919 — feat(cli): --append-system-prompt (L). Adds --append-system-prompt, --append-system-prompt-file, and GEMINI_APPEND_SYSTEM_MD. Fills a real gap: today GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD replaces the entire prompt, so adding one line of project context means forking the whole thing.

  3. #20406 — perf(core): memory management for large tool output (XL). Writes oversized shell output to disk instead of buffering in memory, fixing V8 OOM in truncation paths. Long-running and high-impact for large-repo users.

  4. #23917 — feat(ui): StyleSpan abstraction (XL). Replaces per-character toStyledCharacters() allocation with run-length encoding, targeting 280MB+ heap bloat in complex TableRenderer scenarios.

  5. #29910 — fix(acp): MCP metadata in permission requests + client trust (M). Populates toolCall._meta['gemini-cli'].mcp with server/tool names and lets ACP clients pre-authorize client-supplied MCP servers via _meta.trust — important for editor-integrated deployments.

  6. #29778 — fix(acp): truncate tool output before sending to the model (M). truncateToolOutputThreshold was never applied in --acp mode, so one large shell output could blow the input limit with a 400. Closes a notable ACP-vs-CLI behavioral divergence.

  7. #29783 — P1 fix(core): match include patterns for read_many_files assets (M). Replaces substring checks with real pattern matching; previously any textual overlap could inline binary assets the user never requested.

  8. #29782 — P1 fix(core): null check for exit code in sandbox denial heuristic (S). exitCode !== undefined was always true for null, so every null-exit result entered the denial branch. Small diff, security-relevant correctness fix.

  9. #29912 — fix(core): strip trailing punctuation/unbalanced brackets from web_fetch URLs (M). new URL() happily accepts a trailing comma, so comma-separated URL lists produced polluted URLs and downstream failures.

  10. #29779 — fix(core): mark failed ripgrep searches as tool errors (M). RipGrepTool returned failures without setting error, so the scheduler recorded them as successes while telling the model the search failed — a silent-truth-divergence bug of the same family as #22323.

Also merged/closed or in flight: #29890 (only restore workspace dirs after a successful resume), #29746 (PowerShell substitution quote tracking), #29785 (dispatch final Code Assist SSE event at EOS), #29902 (docs: commandPrefix matches command names, not effects — recommends allow-lists for unattended runs).

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this window, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Subagent orchestration & observability. The largest cluster by far: accurate termination semantics (#22323), trajectory visibility in /chat share (#22598), discovery via settings.json (#18285), shared memory / parallel collaboration (#18287), and agent self-awareness of its own flags and hotkeys (#21432). The through-line is make multi-agent runs inspectable and trustworthy.
  • Context and token frugality. AST-aware reads/search/mapping (#22745, #22746, #22747) and "Tactful Extraction" surgical read hierarchies (#19561) both target the ~36.6k-token-per-turn baseline and the +15k/turn blowups from firehose file reads.
  • Sandboxing over restriction. #19873 argues for zero-dependency OS sandboxing plus post-execution intent routing so the model can use native bash idioms safely; #22672 asks for guardrails against destructive commands; #18397 asks for per-workspace (not global) policy scoping.
  • Out-of-context persistent state. #18836 and #21000 both push task tracking out of the prompt and onto the filesystem (or native file tools) to avoid context rot and session-loss.
  • Smarter tool scoping. #24246 asks the agent to reason about which tools are enabled rather than blindly attaching everything and hitting a 400.
  • Terminal UX as a first-class surface. Flicker-free resize (#21924) and OSC 7501 status reporting (#29918) reflect users running many concurrent CLI sessions.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • False success reporting. The single most corrosive pattern in the tracker: MAX_TURNS surfacing as GOAL success (#22323), Wayland browser failures also reporting GOAL (#21983), and ripgrep failures recorded as successes (#29779). Developers cannot trust exit signals, which breaks automation and evals.
  • Indefinite hangs with no timeout or diagnostic. Generalist-agent delegation (#21409) and interactive prompts such as vite create (#22465) stall until manually cancelled; users report waiting an hour. The only known fix is disabling the feature.
  • Configuration that is silently ignored. Browser Agent skips settings.json overrides like maxTurns (#22267), symlinked agent files are not discovered (#20079), and truncateToolOutputThreshold was a no-op in ACP mode (#29778). Config surface diverges from config behavior.
  • Escaping and quoting edge cases. Incorrect \n handling (#22466), PowerShell substitution quote desync (#29746), and URL tokenization (#29912) all stem from naive string handling around shell and text boundaries.
  • Platform-specific breakage. Wayland (#21983), Thai/Lao SARA AM width (nightly fix), and Windows quoting continue to generate their own issue stream — cross-platform parity is a persistent tax.
  • Memory and rendering overhead. Large tool output causing OOM (#20406), per-character allocations in table rendering (#23917), and resize flicker (#21924) point at the TUI's scaling limits.
  • Workspace hygiene and blast radius. Temporary scripts scattered across directories (#23571) and destructive git operations (#22672) make unattended runs hard to clean up and hard to trust.
  • Extensibility gaps in the prompt layer. The absence of a non-destructive system-prompt append (addressed by #29919) forced users to replace the entire prompt for a one-line project instruction.

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-10-25

Today's Highlights

There were no new releases in the last 24 hours, and the community's attention is almost entirely consumed by a widespread free-tier quota failure: users on both v1 and v2, CLI and Desktop, report "Free usage exceeded" errors despite zero usage, with the 86,400-second cooldown looping back to zero instead of resetting. In parallel, maintainers landed a dense batch of core reliability PRs covering session integrity, subagent result reporting, graceful shutdown, and catalog/ETag optimization.

Releases

No new releases published in the last 24 hours.

Hot Issues

  1. [#58831] Free quota timeout never recovers, sawtooths at 86400s — link The clearest reproduction of the current quota bug: the countdown reaches zero and immediately resets to 86,400s. This is the canonical thread for the entitlement-reset failure affecting all free users.

  2. [#58830] Free usage limit has not reset for two consecutive days in v1 and v2 — link Confirms the regression spans both major versions, ruling out a v2-only migration issue. After one successful request, every free model fails — a strong signal the per-account usage counter is being persisted or read incorrectly.

  3. [#58828] "OpenCode is genuinely broken and HAS to be fixed IMMEDIATELY" — link A high-frustration escalation reporting instant quota exhaustion on Go and Zen models with an 86,400s wait even for users without a subscription. Illustrates how the quota bug is now driving churn and hostile reports.

  4. [#58781] Free Usage Exceeded on all free models in OpenCode Desktop 1.19.4 — link The most-upvoted issue in this window (👍 5). The Desktop-specific angle plus vote count makes it the best proxy for broader user sentiment on the free tier.

  5. [#58605] "Free usage exceeded" after a week of inactivity (Desktop) — link Adds a telling detail: the retry timer reads "retrying in 72970s - attempt no. 1," suggesting malformed remaining-quota or expiry timestamps rather than a genuine usage count.

  6. [#58827] Usage limit hit before any prompts were submitted — link Zero-prompt exhaustion is the strongest evidence that the check is failing before any request is made — i.e., an entitlement/auth lookup failure, not over-consumption.

  7. [#58724] Manual compaction omits required recent, permanently bricking the session — link Serious data-integrity bug: schema decode rejects the persisted compaction message, so every subsequent read fails and forks are also poisoned — with no in-app recovery. High impact for long-running sessions.

  8. [#58527] Permission "ask" silently allows edit/write — link A security-relevant bug: ask renders an approval dialog for shell but behaves as allow for edit/write. Silent file writes in a tool that promises explicit consent is a trust-breaker.

  9. [#52925] opencode api get truncates stdout when piped — link Breaks the canonical opencode api get ... | jq workflow on large (~580 KB) responses while file redirection works fine. Long-lived since Oct 3 and still open — a scripting/CI blocker.

  10. [#58533] Desktop custom-provider dialog writes V1 keys the V2 server ignores — link Representative of the v1→v2 migration class of failures: config written in the old shape produces a confusing "provider not available on this server" toast. Worth highlighting alongside #58529 (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free infinite loop) and #57931 (expired free model blocking the whole catalog), which share the "one bad model poisons the catalog" pattern.

Also notable: #55077 — GPT-6.1 Sol context window raised to 628k in v2.0.28 but still short of the advertised 1.05M; #58558 — hard-coded 1s discovery timeout silently returns zero models for remote Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM endpoints (closed); #58559 — Windows %temp% relocation crashes the CLI (closed).

Key PR Progress

  1. [#58820] perf(core): resize images in a worker, release photon memory when idle — link Eliminates a 420–460 ms server freeze per large image and reclaims ~250 MB of retained WASM memory by moving resizing off the main thread and idling the worker after 10s. Strong win for Desktop/web responsiveness.

  2. [#58817] fix(cli): bound server shutdown with a 10s deadline — link Teardown could previously hang forever after SIGTERM/SIGINT with no indication of the stuck step. Now logs pending work and exits 1, with second-signal handling.

  3. [#58825] fix(core): report a background subagent's later turns to its parent — link Fixes parents receiving "Subagent completed without a text response" when a child went idle and was later woken by a plugin or synthetic message — a correctness fix for multi-agent orchestration.

  4. [#58811] fix(schema): validate base64 attachments in linear time — link Replaces a catastrophic-backtracking-prone regex that ran on every stored message decode (history reload, inbox twice, projector, GET messages). Meaningful latency and hardening improvement.

  5. [#58813] fix(core): revalidate the models.dev catalog with its ETag — link The 5-minute refresh never sent If-None-Match, re-downloading and parsing the full ~6 MB raw (~413 KB brotli) catalog every cycle despite a 304 being available.

  6. [#55146] fix(core): use session transport for foreground compaction — link Foreground summary compaction was sending HTTP even when the selected model uses WebSocket. Directly relevant to the compaction-related breakage seen in #58724.

  7. [#58790] fix(ai): add compatibility.omitEmptyTools to drop empty tools arrays — link Addresses providers that reject requests where the effective tool set is empty but history contains tool calls/results — a common cross-provider interop failure.

  8. [#58788] fix(core): preserve file mode when patch move emulates rename — link "Move to" is implemented as write-then-delete, silently losing permissions on the destination. Important for scripts and executables touched by the agent.

  9. [#58800] perf(core): skip integration list rebuilds when nothing changed — link Every session step rebuilt the integration list multiple times, decoding all stored credentials each pass. Caching fix reduces per-step overhead noticeably.

  10. [#58310] fix(cli): retain Windows binaries across volumes — link Retention fails with EXDEV when package and cache live on different Windows volumes; complements the %temp%-relocation crash in #58559.

Also merged/closed: #58815 (stop leaking service XDG_STATE_HOME into tool shells, name the port owner), #58758 (replace experimental evaluation with Decision), #58771/#58770 (error classification for Google Interactions and AWS restJson1), plus docs updates #58791 (MiMo Code moved to validated clients) and #58823 (Luminary memory plugin).

Feature Request Trends

  • Theme/customization extensibility — #58824 asks for theme overrides and language-token extensions on built-in themes (Catppuccin Mocha, Tokyo Night) rather than fixed scope mappings. Users want to extend themes without forking them.
  • Better multi-agent observability — #58809 requests showing each subagent's effective model and reasoning effort in the Desktop v2 running-subagents list. As subagent orchestration grows, so does demand for visibility into what children are actually doing.
  • Tighter turn control / steering semantics — #58776 proposes conditional steering admission with an expected-turn guard, so corrections are only admitted when the session still owns the turn.
  • Schema clarity for tool-calling models — #55504 notes sessionID is optional in TypeScript but serialized such that models treat it as required, pushing toward more explicit JSON Schema generation.

Developer Pain Points

  1. Free-tier entitlement checks are the dominant failure mode. At least a dozen issues in this window (#58536, #58550, #58553, #58557, #58605, #58781, #58827, #58828, #58829, #58830, #58831, #58832) report quota exhaustion with zero or one request. Reports span CLI v2.1.1, Desktop 1.19.4 and v2, and multiple regions/IPs — pointing at a server-side counter or entitlement lookup rather than client overuse. The non-resetting 86,400s timer and "retrying in 72970s" suggest timestamp handling is also broken.

  2. v1 → v2 migration is still rough. Config written in V1 shape (provider, npm, options) is silently ignored by the V2 server (#58533), and users migrating specifically to escape v1 quota bugs hit API-key expiry on fresh keys (#58832).

  3. Version/config drift creates brittle behavior. Hard-coded 1-second discovery timeouts (#58558), expired free models invalidating the entire catalog (#57931), and stale model metadata (#55077) all show a need for graceful degradation instead of all-or-nothing failure.

  4. Data integrity and consent guarantees are being questioned. A manual compaction can permanently brick a session (#58724), and ask permissions silently allow file writes (#58527). Both erode confidence in long-running agent workflows.

  5. Windows and shell edge cases persist. %temp% relocation crashes the CLI (#58559), cross-volume binary retention fails with EXDEV (#58310), and Nushell PATH setup was only recently supported (#51227).

  6. Scriptability gaps. opencode api get truncating piped output (#52925) blocks the standard | jq and CI-automation patterns — a small fix with outsized impact for tooling users.
