A cluster of 1.3.0/1.4.0 terminal regressions (Windows CSI leakage, Ctrl+Shift+C prompt loss, Alacritty IME autocomplete) was triaged and mostly closed within hours.

2. Releases

Omitted — no releases published in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #4945 — openai-codex connection reliability (OPEN, in-progress, 88 comments, 👍35) The TUI stalls on Working... with no streamed text, no tool call, and no error; Escape is the only recovery. This is the single most-discussed issue in the tracker and the clearest signal that provider-level stream handling still has unbounded-wait paths.

  2. #7730 — High CPU on macOS with long sessions (OPEN, bug, 22 comments, 👍11) 50–110% CPU and 600–800 MB RSS on long sessions, apparently correlated with context size. Community is treating this as the practical ceiling on multi-hour agent use.

  3. #6665 — TUI pins a full core while streaming (OPEN, in-progress, 15 comments, 👍7) Reproduces with pi -ne, so the cause is core, not extension: uncached Intl.Segmenter grapheme segmentation plus a full Markdown rebuild per chunk. A spindump-backed diagnosis makes this one of the most actionable perf reports open.

  4. #11157 — sendMessage at session_start turns every session into a legacy transcript (OPEN, prio:p0, in-progress) getInitialSystemMessage reads messages[0]; extensions like pi-memory and pi-session-search inject ahead of it, so Anthropic requests silently lose the system field. A p0 correctness bug caused entirely by extension ordering.

  5. #8643 — Bedrock: OpenAI models reject images nested in toolResult.content (OPEN, 14 comments, 👍5) Requests hoisting tool-result images into sibling user blocks, matching what openai-completions.ts already does. Notably, the reporter says a fix + regression test are ready but the prior PR (#8642) was auto-closed by the contribution gate.

  6. #8810 — Extension-registered providers intermittently ignore defaultProvider/defaultModel (OPEN, 9 comments, 👍5) Fresh sessions fall back to another provider's default when the provider comes from pi.registerProvider(). Nondeterminism here undermines trust in the extension provider API.

  7. #10157 — Gemini thought signatures dropped on the AI Studio OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OPEN) extra_content.google.thought_signature is returned on tool calls but not replayed, breaking multi-turn reasoning for Gemini Flash Lite via AI Studio.

  8. #10390 — Anthropic SSE parser mishandles CRLF split across chunks (OPEN, bug) \r and \n arriving in separate chunks are treated as two line breaks, flushing an event with no data:, which throws Unexpected end of JSON input and aborts the turn. A classic transport-boundary bug with a narrow but fatal blast radius.

  9. #11221 — Pi doesn't pick up refreshed AWS credentials in long-running sessions (OPEN, bug) Bedrock sessions longer than the STS token lifetime fail with ExpiredTokenException even when a background refresher is running. Pairs with #10390 as evidence that long-lived session credential/transport handling needs an owner.

  10. #11379 — Ctrl+Shift+C loses the prompt being typed (CLOSED, bug) A 1.3.0 regression that users described as "driving me crazy angry": copying from output eats the in-progress prompt. Closed within a day, along with sibling terminal-hygiene issues #11377 (stripAnsi leaking private-parameter CSI) and #11205 (Windows PowerShell flooded with mouse/focus reports).

Also closed this cycle: #9265 (O(n²) tool-call argument re-parsing in openai-completions streaming) and #10642 (embedded SDK session memory never dropping) — both marked CLOSED without action, despite describing concrete production blockers for embedded/multi-session hosts.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #11368 — refactor provider definitions (OPEN) Replaces generate-models.ts with one defineProvider() file per built-in provider, shared model-family rules (Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, Kimi, Google), and models.dev v2 API adapters. The foundation for the four stacked PRs below.

  2. #11369 — Alibaba Model Studio + Z.AI pay-as-you-go providers (OPEN) Adds alibaba, alibaba-cn (DashScope international/China) and Z.AI PAYG alongside the plans pi already ships.

  3. #11370 — DeepInfra, Nebius, Ollama Cloud, Scaleway, SiliconFlow, StepFun (OPEN) Six hosted inference providers selected by models.dev contributor activity and issue-tracker demand; DeepInfra alone contributes 74 models.

  4. #11371 — Claude models on Google Vertex AI (OPEN) google-vertex now lists 13 non-deprecated Claude models via Vertex's Anthropic Messages API, implemented by reusing the Anthropic Messages code with a fetch wrapper.

  5. #11372 — Route non-Converse Bedrock models through Bedrock Mantle (OPEN) Fixes #5363 for Bedrock API keys: 16 listed models (GPT-5.4→GPT-6.1, gpt-oss, Grok 4.3/4.6, Gemma 4) are only served on Mantle, the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and were being rejected by Converse as invalid identifiers.

  6. #11355 — Kimi Coding K3.1 Pro support (CLOSED) Derives the K3 wire preset from parsed effort metadata rather than a model-ID list; K3.1 Pro/Highspeed now expose low/high/max, send reasoning_effort, preserve reasoning content, and keep dynamically loaded tools out of the top-level tool list.

  7. #9329 — Detect Orca terminals as Kitty-image capable (OPEN) Treats TERM_PROGRAM=Orca as supporting Kitty inline images, true color, and OSC 8 hyperlinks so image components stop falling back to text.

  8. #11363 — fullscreenCopyTarget setting for primary selection (CLOSED) Lets fullscreen copy-on-select target the X11/Wayland primary buffer (middle-click paste) instead of the clipboard — directly relevant to the copy/paste friction in #11379.

  9. #10135 — Normalise compaction usage to prevent footer crash on resume (CLOSED) Stops persisting raw provider summaryUsage on both passthrough branches, fixing a crash when resuming a compacted session.

  10. #11341 — Clear error for unusable proxy URLs (CLOSED) HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY values undici can't parse (e.g. socks5h://, missing scheme, URLs with paths) now exit with a readable message instead of an undici Invalid URL protocol stack trace.

5. Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #11306 — pi-continuity: auto-resume after coding-plan usage limits and interrupted turns Built around OpenAI's 5-hour usage limit, which halts a run and previously required manual "continue" hours later. Pi already retries transient provider errors and compacts on context overflow, but usage limits — a distinct failure class — had no handling.

Community feedback

  • #11356 — Before 1.0 vs after 1.0 (rip) The author argues baseline context consumption regressed post-1.0, with "one single Hello" approaching limits and Pi feeling closer to opencode in prompt overhead. Only 👍1, but it echoes the context-efficiency concerns in #7730 and #10642.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Provider breadth and correct routing. The dominant theme by volume: new pay-as-you-go providers (#11369), hosted inference endpoints (#11370), Claude on Vertex (#11371), Mantle routing for Bedrock (#11372), and effort-aware model presets (#11355). The direction is a declarative per-provider catalog rather than generated lists.
  • Multi-modal payload correctness across providers. Hoisting tool-result images for Bedrock/OpenAI (#8643), using file_id references instead of replaying base64 for Codex (#8617), and preserving Gemini thought signatures (#10157) are all the same underlying ask: a provider-agnostic content model that adapters translate faithfully.
  • Extension API surface for real products. A Code Mode output writer for host-owned storage (#11070), watchEvents resume from a last-seen entry (#11327), deterministic provider defaults (#8810), and composable compaction with span args, summary-model override, and entry refs (#11310).
  • Long-lived / embedded session lifecycle. Durable execution semantics (#11139, #11327), memory reclamation after compaction (#10642), and credential refresh (#11221) point at a server-hosted-many-sessions use case that the current SDK doesn't yet fully support.
  • Terminal/UI ergonomics. Kitty image support in more terminals (#9329), primary-selection copy target (#11363), IME commit handling (#11177), and clean escape-sequence stripping (#11377).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Streaming performance is the top blocker for long sessions. Two of the three highest-engagement issues (#6665, #7730) describe a full core pinned during streaming, with root causes traced to per-chunk Markdown rebuilds, uncached grapheme segmentation, and (previously, #9265) quadratic tool-argument re-parsing. Embedded hosts feel this hardest because a blocked event loop stalls every co-hosted session.
  • Provider integrations break on edge-case transports and payload shapes. Stalled streams with no error (#4945), CRLF split across chunks (#10390), dropped thought signatures (#10157), rejected nested images (#8643), and stale AWS credentials (#11221) are all "works until it doesn't" failures that surface mid-turn and are hard to diagnose from the TUI.
  • Extension ecosystem fragility. Extensions that register providers, send messages at session_start, or reload mid-session can silently change core behavior — losing the Anthropic system field (#11157), breaking all subsequent requests with tool_reference_unresolved (#11376), or flipping a session onto the wrong default model (#8810).
  • Terminal compatibility regressions keep recurring. The 1.3.0 rollout produced a burst of UI-hygiene bugs: prompt loss on Ctrl+Shift+C (#11379), CSI mouse/focus payloads leaking into PowerShell (#11205), stripAnsi leaving private-parameter sequences (#11377), and Alacritty IME autocomplete failures (#11177).
  • Triage throughput vs. contributor intent. Several closed-without-action issues (#9265, #10642, #11310, #10145, #8642) came with prototypes, patches, or production impact, and #8643 explicitly notes a prior PR was auto-closed by the contribution gate. Combined with many untriaged items closed the same day they were filed, the perceived review bar is a recurring source of friction.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-10-25

1. Today's Highlights

Qwen Code shipped v0.26.1, a small patch release headlined by a breaking fix that restores per-group session isolation for QQ bot channels, alongside daemon token persistence in the Desktop build. CI infrastructure continues to dominate community activity, with a cluster of issues around runner capacity, main-push failure reporting, and the Managed Agent gate consuming the most discussion. On the code side, security hardening (symlink escapes, read-only file atomic writes) and cost-accounting correctness (reasoning-token double counting) drew multiple competing PRs today.

2. Releases

v0.26.1 (qwen-code)

  • Breaking change: fix(qqbot)!: restore per-group session isolation under thread scope (#13882, @Eric-GoodBoy-Tech) — corrects sessionScope: "chat_thread" behavior where direct messages were incorrectly treated as shared sessions (see also closed issue #14350).
  • Release notes are currently a stub (qwen-release-notes:v1); the complete change list is deferred to the linked release.

desktop-v0.26.1

  • feat(serve): add daemon token persistence (#15023, @wenshao).
  • fix(release): cover every spawned vendored binary — release packaging hardening for bundled binaries.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #13395 — tracking(runtime): Kubernetes tool runtime progress and cross-platform delivery gates (23 comments, in-progress) The longest-running design tracker in the repo. Two S1 root causes are now implemented in Draft #15457 and locally validated, but the issue stays open pending full CI and native ACK re-testing. The high comment count reflects sustained reviewer scrutiny over an extended period.

  2. #15446 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, HostedPublicWorkspaceIT.publicShellReceiptFaultsNeverRepeatEffects (+12 more) (14 comments) The single largest CI failure cluster today. Repeated fault-gate failures in the Java hosted workspace suite are throttling merge velocity and generating noise across the issue tracker.

  3. #13113 — Session becomes unopenable: "Transcript snapshot is too large to index" (9 comments, P1) file_history_snapshot grows quadratically in long sessions, eventually exceeding a hardcoded 256 MiB index limit and rendering the session permanently unopenable. A clear data-loss-adjacent severity issue with strong community interest.

  4. #14859 — ci: track runner capacity and independent main validation (9 comments) The author explicitly retracts earlier percentage estimates and replaces them with a corrected capacity model. Signals that CI runner scarcity is now a first-class project concern rather than an isolated annoyance.

  5. #15056 — feat: local /autofix-pr to watch a PR and fix CI failures, review feedback, and conflicts (5 comments) Proposes a session-local command that polls a PR, distinguishes code fixes from infrastructure re-runs, and iterates until green. Resonates strongly given the CI failure volume above.

  6. #15479 — Auto-memory bound to the startup directory breaks multi-workspace sessions (4 comments, new) Multi-project solution folders cannot write memory to the correct per-project store; everything lands in the global store. Directly affects anyone using Qwen Code across a monorepo or solution folder.

  7. #10879 — hk4 pinned as release host but still carries the shared ecs-qwen label (4 comments, P1) Release validation jobs compete with ordinary PR CI on the same host, causing timing-sensitive sharded test failures. A long-lived (since Sept 3) infra defect with a precise root cause.

  8. #13895 — modelFallbacks chain skipped when a 429 body carries an unrecognized error.code (4 comments) The fallback chain never engages when a provider returns a rate-limit error with a non-standard code, because it is classified as a fail-fast client error. High practical impact for multi-provider failover setups.

  9. #15445 — Web Shell fails to load in non-English browsers (3 comments, need-retesting) desktopRelay i18n lookup has no fallback, throwing TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'desktopRelay.trigger') for any locale outside English/Chinese. Regressed in 0.26.0 and completely blocks the UI — a small code gap with outsized user impact.

  10. #15470 — ci: main-push failures file no issues; reporter drops them as superseded (3 comments) Ten main-push failures between 14:00Z and 17:30Z on 2026-10-24 produced zero issues, because the reporter waits on a slow hosted runner and then treats its own report as superseded. Undermines CI observability.

Also worth watching: #15444 (reasoning tokens double-counted in cost display), #15418 (managed automation scanner blocks its single thread per gate probe), #15461 (release-host provisioning on the idle hz ARM64 pool).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #15319 — feat(web-shell): move no-workspace sessions beside workspaces Promotes no-workspace sessions to their own peer group between Workspaces and Archived, with independently persisted collapse state. Fixes the case where collapsing Workspaces hid these sessions entirely.

  2. #15386 — fix(cli): preserve checkpoint restore ownership and cold continuation Restores Ink checkpoints through the real tool scheduler, pairs replay results with the original logical call, and rejects stale owners. Important for checkpoint/rewind reliability.

  3. #15030 — feat(cli): raise workspace skill install limits Splits the transport ceiling from the on-disk ceiling for ZIP, GitHub, and local-folder skill installs, replacing a single hardcoded 6 MiB / 6 MiB / 2 MiB-per-file / 128-file budget in place since July.

  4. #15261 — feat(runtime-broker): add HTTP-backed external scratch workers Adds an opt-in external-scratch Runtime provider that delegates session worker placement to an operator-run HTTP service, with deterministic request handles, attestation, and retry semantics. The most substantial runtime extensibility change in flight.

  5. #12585 — fix(acp): persist embedded text resources for transcript replay Persists bounded original ACP embedded text resource blocks with their owning user prompt and replays them as typed user chunks, exposing them separately from resource_link attachments in the daemon UI SDK.

  6. #15453 — fix(core): respect read-only files and hard links in atomic writes Atomic replace now checks destination writability before committing and preserves hard-link identity. A meaningful correctness/security fix for file-editing tools.

  7. #15430 — fix(core): reject symlink escapes in memory imports Canonicalizes both the imported path and allowed roots before containment checks, closing a path-traversal hole where a committed symlink could pull in files outside the project.

  8. #12222 — feat(core,cli): add toolParametersMandatory opt-in for strict OpenAI-compatible servers When enabled, zero-argument tools are sent with an explicit empty "parameters": {"type":"object","properties":{}} instead of omitting the field. Directly unblocks users of stricter OpenAI-compatible backends.

  9. #15472 / #15464 — fix: stop double-counting reasoning tokens in cost estimates Two independent implementations of the same fix (from the issue author and a maintainer) that derive billable output from the aggregate total rather than always adding candidates + thoughts. Both preserve Gemini-style disjoint thoughts accounting.

  10. #15485 — fix(ci): retry transient npm publishes in the release step Retries recursive npm publish up to four times with 30/60/90 s backoff and revalidates registry metadata each attempt. Paired with #15471 (file main-CI failures even when the successor run hasn't settled), this directly targets today's release/CI reliability theme.

Also notable: #15433 (preserve OpenAI cache_write_tokens for OTel provenance), #15190 (extend daemon PATH on macOS when Desktop is launched from Finder/Dock), #15274 / #15286 / #15275 (narrow the self-hosted SDK Java Maven host lock to cache write-back only).

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this period, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • CI/PR automation inside the agent — /autofix-pr (#15056) plus the managed automation scanner throughput work (#15418) point toward letting Qwen Code own the full PR lifecycle: watch, diagnose, fix, retry infrastructure, resolve conflicts.
  • Multi-workspace / multi-project memory — #15479 requests git-root-keyed memory stores so solution folders spanning several projects stop polluting the global store.
  • Runtime and sandbox portability — the Kubernetes tool runtime tracker (#13395) and external scratch workers (#15261) reflect demand for pluggable, operator-hosted execution backends.
  • OpenAI-compatible provider compatibility — strict tool schema handling (#12222) and correct 429 classification for fallback chains (#13895) are recurring asks from users running non-Qwen endpoints.
  • Cost and token transparency — reasoning-token accounting (#15444) and OpenAI cache-write token provenance (#15433) signal growing interest in accurate billing/telemetry.
  • Desktop/daemon polish — daemon token persistence (shipped), macOS PATH inheritance (#15190), and Web Shell i18n fallback (#15445).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI capacity and reliability is the top friction point. Runner contention (#14859, #10879, #15461), noisy Managed Agent gate failures (#15446, #14724, #14784), and a failure reporter that silently files nothing (#15470) combine into slow feedback loops and untracked regressions. Multiple fixes this cycle target the Maven host lock scope and publish retries specifically.
  • Session scaling limits. A hardcoded 256 MiB transcript index cap plus quadratic snapshot growth (#13113) can permanently brick a long-running session — a hard failure mode with no recovery path.
  • Silent failure classification. Errors that look like rate limits but carry vendor-specific codes are treated as permanent client errors, bypassing fallbacks (#13895). Users discover this only after a task dies mid-run.
  • Cost reporting inaccuracy. Reasoning tokens counted twice for OpenAI-style providers (#15444) erodes trust in the cost display.
  • Last-mile UX gaps that fully block usage. A missing i18n fallback makes the Web Shell unusable for every non-English/Chinese locale (#15445) — small in code, total in impact.
  • Deferred-review debt. A recurring pattern of "follow-up" issues carrying non-blocking review suggestions (#14973, #13698, #14625, #12986) shows review throughput outpacing merge-and-cleanup capacity.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-10-25

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-10-25 00:29 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-10-25

数据说明：所提供数据集覆盖过去 24 小时内更新的 500 个 Issue 和 500 个 PR。PR 评论数未填充，因此下文 PR 排名使用标签、状态和所述影响，而非评论量。

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 仍是高速迭代项目：过去 24 小时内有 500 个 Issue 和 500 个 PR 更新，其中 92 个 Issue 关闭、259 个 PR 合并或关闭。发布了两个版本——一个聚焦可重放安全会话恢复的补丁版本，以及一个扩展稳定/LTS 网关版本，包含安全与可靠性回移。活动重心明显偏向回归与稳定性工作，而非净新增功能，尤其集中在插件源码捕获、SQLite/状态管理、会话恢复和 Windows 更新流程。项目健康度喜忧参半：维护者吞吐强劲，且存在 LTS 通道，但仍有多个 P0/P1 回归未关闭，包括数据集中评论数最高的 Issue。stale 与 needs-maintainer-review 标签的数量表明，主要瓶颈是评审带宽，而非贡献者兴趣。

2. 发布

v2026.10.7

  • 重点： 可重放安全的会话恢复。
  • 值得注意的变更：
    • 中断的会话会保留恢复来源信息与未完成的工具结果。
    • 已停止的对话在接受下一条消息前会清理终端恢复残留。
    • 被拒绝的 Claude CLI 草稿不会进入最终回复。
    • 更多大型变更说明在提供的数据中被截断。
  • 破坏性变更 / 迁移： 摘录中未提供明确的破坏性变更或迁移步骤。鉴于会话状态与恢复逻辑的变更，运维人员应在升级后验证中断会话与工具结果行为。
  • 链接：OpenClaw releases

v2026.9.34

  • 通道： 仅 Gateway 的 extended-stable，被描述为当前 LTS 等价通道。
  • 内容： 2026 年 9 月底的 OpenClaw，加上关键安全更新、可靠性与性能修复，以及新模型支持。
  • 建议： 适合优先考虑稳定性、而非 2026.10 功能线的生产/LTS 用户。
  • 链接：OpenClaw releases

Beta 信号： PR #182951 引用了 v2026.10.10-beta.3，表明此处列出的最新稳定版之外仍有活跃的 beta 通道。

3. 项目进展

过去 24 小时有 259 个 PR 合并或关闭，进展集中在可靠性、性能和 UI 协作：

  • 会话/状态性能： #182934（已关闭）跨投影共享常驻 actor 条目，减少重复的解码会话条目。
  • 提及/收件箱架构： #155419（已关闭）将 Inbox 数据库工作移出 Gateway 线程；#153812（已关闭）在 UI 中新增会话提及通知。
  • 打包/更新可靠性： #182982（已关闭）恢复打包后 update、MCP 和文件传输 helper 的独立启动。
  • CLI 卡顿修复： #182984（已关闭）避免 CLI 打开已被 Gateway 持有的 agent 数据库时进行长达数分钟的 SQLite integrity_check 扫描。
  • 待合并 P0 修复： #182951 将 config set/patch/unset 路由到正在运行的 Gateway，修复 v2026.10.10-beta.3 中退出码 1 的回归。
  • 性能 PR 队列： #183034 减少 transcript turn 数据库往返；#183042 在冷启动期间延迟休眠 Chat 工作；#182976 在冷历史核算中复用已验证的条目事实。
  • 通道可靠性： #183028 修复 Telegram ask_user 问题在进度草稿退役期间被丢弃的问题。
  • Provider/运行时： #176567 修复 Bun 上 OpenAI 实时语音 socket 绕过托管代理的问题；#180599 使 Code Mode 运行过期时间保持在单调时钟上。

主题： 合并/开放的 PR 集合显示出明确方向：减少数据库往返、改善冷启动 UI 行为，并加固会话/提及投递。功能工作相对于稳定 2026.9/2026.10 回归而言是次要的。

4. 社区热点

最活跃 Issue

  1. #160959 — P0: Gateway blocks for minutes while capturing large external plugins — 50 条评论，崩溃循环，no-new-fix-pr。

    • 自 2026.9.6 引入插件生成捕获以来，带大型外部/工作区插件的 Gateway 会在启动时以及准备好的模型运行时重新发布时阻塞事件循环数分钟。
    • 底层需求： 插件捕获必须异步/有界，并支持复用与原生二进制处理。这是数据集中最清晰的子系统级回归。

  2. #164294 — P2: Gateway state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes — 30 条评论。

    • WAL checkpoint 被进程内读取器永久阻塞；checkpointedFrames=866 对 logFrames=17091。
    • 底层需求： SQLite 读取器生命周期管理与可观测的 checkpoint 诊断。

  3. #159356 — P2: llama.cpp manager reports ready while embedding child exits — 29 条评论。

    • 子进程退出后，嵌入请求返回 HTTP 500；怀疑存在内存压力，但尚未确认。
    • 底层需求： 本地模型子进程的进程监督与就绪语义。

  4. #157989 — P1: Plugin source capture rewrites 1.1–1.4 GB per CLI command and ~6.5 GB per Gateway start — 23 条评论。

    • 对外部插件重复进行字节复制和 SHA-256 哈希造成严重 SSD 磨损。
    • 底层需求： 捕获缓存/复用，并排除捆绑的原生二进制文件。

  5. #53408 — P2: Write/exec tool parameters silently dropped after long conversations — 15 条评论，2 👍，自 2026 年 3 月起 stale。

    • 在 15+ 轮大量工具使用后，write 和 exec 到达时参数对象为空。
    • 底层需求： 长会话工具调用序列化完整性——一个长期存在的信任问题。

值得关注的活跃 PR

  • #182951 — P0: Route config mutations through a running Gateway
  • #176567 — P1: OpenAI realtime voice proxy on Bun
  • #182066 — perf(cron): reuse source validation at transcript target checks — 可供维护者查看
  • #183034 — improve(sessions): reduce transcript turn DB round trips

分析： 前四大 Issue 中有三个（#160959、#157989、#162585）共享同一个插件源码捕获根因。SQLite/状态数据库生命周期问题构成第二集群（#164294、#164948、#175926、#181660）。社区受到少量子系统的过度影响，因此定向修复具有高杠杆效应。

  • #150598 — Completion-wake delivery semantics（P2）：针对多会话编排中仅终端、新回合、合并以及失败按分诊处理的投递语义，提出基于现场数据的方案。

7. 用户反馈摘要

主要痛点

  • 运营成本与硬件磨损： 插件源码捕获导致每条命令和每次 Gateway 启动产生 GB 级写入（#157989、#162585）。Matrix E2EE 空闲时约 50% CPU 和约 52 MB/分钟写入（#154104）。
  • Windows 上更新/安装脆弱： 反复自动更新失败、未展开的 $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR、被放弃的更新记录，以及修复期间租约丢失（#157812、#182476）。
  • 会话可靠性与消息丢失： 原生关闭失败后 agent 执行被锁定（#159789）；子代理最终文本丢失（#154299）；Telegram 公告过期（#158154）；崩溃恢复可能使 agent 不可用（#166634）。
  • 信任/安全担忧： 精选记忆文件可能被永久静默排除（#153426）；带凭据的 CDP URL 进入面向模型的输出（#158966）；Talk 通话丢失调用方权限（#167876）。
  • 成本可见性： 心跳从不复用 Anthropic prompt 缓存，每次成本约 $0.40–0.95（#161208）。
  • UI 打磨： WebChat transcript 抖动（#164394）、重复/三次渲染（#149912）、可见的内部上下文注入（#165041）、过时的进度 spinner（#137188）。

体现的使用场景

  • 使用子代理、长时间运行后台任务和协调器会话的重度多会话编排。
  • Telegram、Matrix 和 QQ 通道部署，包括论坛主题和 E2EE。
  • CLI 支持的模型（claude-cli、Codex app-server）和本地嵌入栈（llama.cpp）。
  • Windows 桌面/服务器安装和 npm 全局部署。
  • 带原生二进制文件的大型外部插件树。

满意度/不满意度： 用户正在提供详细、高质量的复现和运维变通方案，这表明参与度很高。不满主要集中在 2026.9.x 线引入的回归、Windows 更新可靠性以及长期 stale 的 Issue。extended-stable/LTS 发布对生产用户是一个积极信号。

整体健康评估： OpenClaw 非常活跃，PR 吞吐强劲，并有可信的 LTS 流程，但项目当前正在偿还插件捕获、SQLite/状态生命周期、会话恢复和 Windows 更新方面的显著回归债务。最高杠杆行动是针对插件源码捕获集群（#160959、#157989、#162585）的协调修复，其次是 SQLite WAL/读取器生命周期清理，以及关闭 P0 记忆来源缺口（#153426）。

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告——个人 AI 助手 / Agent OSS 生态

窗口： 2026-10-25 社区摘要。项目： OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw。
健康分： 分析师综合评分（0–10），权重包括发布节奏、Issue/PR 吞吐量、回归/安全负担、评审积压和流程成熟度。并非正式基准。

1. 生态概览

个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态正进入可靠性与治理阶段：项目交付的净新增能力减少，更多精力投入到会话恢复、状态存储生命周期、插件治理、投递保证和升级安全。OpenClaw 仍以网关为中心架构和 LTS 通道保持规模领先，而 Hermes Agent、ZeroClaw 和 QwenPaw 分别围绕桌面会话、SOP/安全工作流和多 Agent 治理占据更窄但可信的位置。跨项目来看，社区反馈主要集中在静默失败、数据持久性、插件/扩展信任、平台特定更新故障以及成本/延迟可见性。IronClaw 在本窗口无活动。最强差异化因素已不再是模型访问，而是运维信任——即会话、记忆、插件、通道和升级能否在生产负载下可预测地运行。

3. OpenClaw 的定位

相较同行的优势

  • 规模与吞吐量： 24 小时内更新 1,000 个 Issue/PR，259 个 PR 合并/关闭，92 个 Issue 关闭。这比 Hermes 和 ZeroClaw 高一个数量级，也远高于 QwenPaw。
  • 发布成熟度： 唯一具备可见的稳定版 + LTS/延长稳定版流程以及活跃 beta 线的项目。Hermes 和 QwenPaw 未发布任何版本；ZeroClaw 的 v0.8.7 已准备但尚未发布。
  • 广度： 网关、提供商、插件、通道、会话恢复、Windows 更新流程、SQLite 状态管理、本地嵌入和命令行工具都在同一生态中活跃。
  • 生态引力： 大型外部插件树、多会话编排、Telegram/Matrix/QQ 部署、CLI 后端模型以及 Windows/npm 安装都在反馈中有所体现。

相较同行的劣势

  • 回归债务： P0 插件源码捕获阻塞（#160959，50 条评论）和 P1 SSD 磨损捕获（#157989）是影响力大但尚未解决的聚类问题；#160959 没有修复 PR。
  • 评审带宽： stale 和 needs-maintainer-review 标签表明瓶颈是评审容量，而非贡献者兴趣。
  • SQLite/状态与 Windows 更新脆弱性： 仍有若干 P0/P1 Issue 围绕 WAL checkpointing、reader lifecycle、崩溃恢复和 OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST。

技术路线差异

  • OpenClaw 是以网关为中心的：长期运行的 Gateway 拥有配置、会话、状态数据库、插件捕获和通道路由。近期工作将配置变更路由到运行中的 Gateway，并改进可重放安全的会话恢复。
  • 同行项目范围更窄：Hermes 偏重桌面/会话生命周期；ZeroClaw 是 Rust/Tauri，带有 SOP、策略和记忆后端；QwenPaw 偏重治理/审计和多 Agent 编排。
  • OpenClaw 的 LTS 通道赋予其生产采用优势，当前数据集中没有同行能匹敌。

会话/状态生命周期与恢复 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw 可重放安全恢复、中断会话溯源、确定性会话关闭、关闭时刷盘恢复、可归因取消、仅追加的会话事件。OpenClaw 存在 SQLite WAL/reader 生命周期问题；Hermes 存在会话标识/标题冲突和无界 DM 会话；QwenPaw 存在 Agent 间静默取消；ZeroClaw 正在探索规范会话事件历史。

安全与供应链加固 ZeroClaw、Hermes、OpenClaw、QwenPaw ZeroClaw 关闭了 RUSTSEC/CA-bundle 问题；Hermes 修复了脱敏和 MCP 工具集扩大问题；OpenClaw 存在携带凭据的 CDP URL 泄漏和调用方权限问题；QwenPaw 存在跨通道记忆轨迹泄漏。共同需求：密钥脱敏、权限边界、依赖安全公告和通道安全输出。

QwenPaw 多 Agent 编排、治理/审计、团队/自托管默认配置、Matrix/QQ/Feishu 通道 自托管团队、多 Agent 集群、合规敏感型部署 policy.yaml + governance/audit.db；hooks；通道集成；ReMe 记忆升级；Console 默认配置
ZeroClaw SOP 引擎、安全/供应链、记忆正确性、shell 策略、邮件/XMPP 通道 注重安全的自托管者、工作流/SOP 操作者、Windows shell 自动化 Rust/Tauri 工作区；策略解析器；SOP 引擎；记忆后端；RUSTSEC/CA 卫生；发布稳定化模式

关键对比： OpenClaw 是广泛平台型选手；Hermes 以桌面/会话体验为主导；ZeroClaw 以安全/工作流为主导；QwenPaw 以多 Agent/治理为主导。OpenClaw 的架构最集中、最面向生产；ZeroClaw 的最偏向安全/控制面；QwenPaw 的最偏向合规/审计；Hermes 的最偏向桌面人体工学。

7. 趋势信号

趋势 跨项目证据 对 AI Agent 开发者的价值
可靠性成为新功能 OpenClaw/Hermes/ZeroClaw/QwenPaw 中的会话恢复、WAL/reader 生命周期、可重放安全事件、关闭刷盘恢复、原子更新 尽早投入幂等副作用、可重放会话日志、状态存储生命周期管理和升级安全迁移。
静默失败不可接受 QwenPaw 配置重置/审计停止/无原因取消；Hermes 静默模型回退和未投递的澄清；OpenClaw 伪成功和内部上下文可见；ZeroClaw 不透明策略拒绝 将结构化审计事件、用户可见诊断、变更日志和显式失败契约构建到 Agent 运行时中。
记忆必须持久且可治理 ZeroClaw S0 Markdown 记忆数据丢失；OpenClaw 溯源排除和压缩前刷盘；QwenPaw 记忆轨迹泄漏 将记忆视为事务型子系统：并发控制、溯源、同意门控、压缩和跨通道输出卫生。
插件生态需要先治理再规模化 Hermes 目录准入/验证分级；OpenClaw 插件捕获性能；ZeroClaw 插件安装清理 尽早定义插件 API 边界、准入策略、沙箱化、扩展面决策以及捕获/缓存行为。
更新/安装可靠性是信任门槛 Hermes state.db 预检阻塞更新；OpenClaw Windows 租约/更新失败；两者均存在 Windows 回归 使用真实用户数据量和平台特定安装程序测试升级；让更新路径原子化且可恢复。
通道投递正成为产品关键 Telegram 过期、Bot Chat 标题冲突、Matrix E2EE 恢复、QQ 流式传输、邮件附件、XMPP 抽象传输层并明确投递语义：重试、重连、去重、附件功能对等和终态确认。
成本/延迟优化正进入核心 OpenClaw 提示词缓存未命中和心跳成本；Hermes 提示词裁剪；ZeroClaw 上下文窗口元数据回退 将缓存感知的提示词组装、模型元数据归一化、限制感知回退以及 token/成本可观测性构建到路由中。
安全加固横跨供应链与运行时 ZeroClaw 中的 RUSTSEC/CA bundle；Hermes 中的脱敏/MCP 工具集扩大；OpenClaw 中的 CDP 凭据泄漏和调用方权限；QwenPaw 中的审计/治理 将依赖安全公告、密钥脱敏、权限边界和审计日志视为一等 Agent 平台功能。
多 Agent 语义需要契约 OpenClaw 子 Agent 投递；Hermes Kanban 重复回调；QwenPaw 集群取消归因；ZeroClaw SOP 完整性 在扩展 Agent 集群前，定义取消归因、副作用幂等性、完成投递语义和失败即分诊行为。

总结： OpenClaw 是该生态的规模与发布流程领导者，但其下一步质量提升取决于解决插件捕获和 SQLite/状态问题簇。Hermes 和 ZeroClaw 是可信的第二梯队项目，拥有强用户参与度，但路线图受评审制约，且尚有未解决的基础设计问题。QwenPaw 拥有真实的生产用户，但必须提升合并吞吐量和静默失败可观测性。在所有活跃项目中，胜出的 Agent 平台将是那些让会话、记忆、插件、通道和升级可观测、可恢复且可信的平台——而不仅仅是功能丰富。

Hermes Agent — 项目摘要，2026-10-25

4. 社区热门话题

1. Issue #50718 — 桌面端会话可见性与通知（12 条评论，3 👍，数据集中互动量最高） 用户无法分辨哪个会话正在运行、已完成还是被阻塞。报告将其拆解为三个独立的根因：后台轮次完成时没有未读提示、没有需要输入的信号，以及没有操作系统级徽标。深层需求： 会话必须成为一等、可观测的对象——当前 UI 是为单一前台聊天优化的，而真实使用场景是多会话且后台化的。

2. Issue #133253 — 桌面端更新被 30 秒的 state.db 预检阻塞（8 条评论，标记为 duplicate） 约 1GB 的 state.db 无法通过硬编码的 spawnSync 超时，因此“立即更新”在触及任何内容之前就被取消。深层需求： 升级路径必须能随用户累积数据而扩展；固定超时对每个长期用户都是潜在故障。

3. Issue #48997 — 显式关闭被弃用的运行时会话及其拥有的后端（6 条评论） 新建聊天、/new、归档、删除、关闭次级窗口以及退出，都会让运行时会话和后端继续存活。深层需求： 定义明确的会话生命周期，并具备确定性的资源回收——这与 #136012 中表现为 DM 无界增长的缺口是同一个问题。

4. Issue #143053 — 插件目录准入指引（4 条评论） 一位维护完整工作流/源码包的第三方维护者找不到受支持的准入途径——并明确表示不是要求绕过安装扫描器。深层需求： 插件生态的发展速度已超过其已发布的治理机制；CoreWeave 验证 PR（#144203）是同一问题从维护者视角的体现。

5. Issue #143715 — Bot Chat 投递被拒 not_found（4 条评论） 一个规范 Bot Chat 标题被未绑定的 tui 来源行占用，导致 profile 投递被永久阻塞。深层需求： 标题/会话键冲突需要一套解决规则，而不是失败即关闭的拒绝。

6. Issue #142839 — model.default 的斜杠前缀被原样转发 → 503 + 静默回退（4 条评论） 当 model.provider 已指明提供方时，<provider>/<model> 仍被原样传给上游，产生 model_not_found 和一个不可见的降级。深层需求： 配置归一化加上禁止静默回退——用户必须知道所选模型未被使用。

7. Issue #18964 — Reticulum/LXMF 消息网关（4 条评论，3 👍） 可见集合中运行时间最长的请求（2026-05-02 开启）：一种与链路无关、无服务器的传输方式。深层需求： 在断网/离网或抗审查环境中的部署。

8. Issue #136189 — P1：关机刷写文件写入了错误的会话键（4 条评论） 关机时排队的消息按适配器隔离标志生成键，而恢复时却通过网关级标志解析，因此当标志不一致时重启恢复永远无法映射到它们。这是数据集中最严重的投递保证缺陷。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

下个周期高概率落地：

  1. 桌面端会话生命周期 + 可观测性 — #50718（未读标记、需要输入的提示、OS 徽标）和 #48997（显式关闭被弃用的会话/后端）。它们属于同一子系统，互动量最高，且也能缓解 #136012。预计会先落地一个范围受限的子集（未读提示 + 需要输入）。
  2. 插件目录治理与分级 — #143053（准入途径）加上今天的 verified 层级 PR（#144203）以及待处理条目：Frihet ERP #134790 / pin #144210、Conxt memory #144192、KAME 1.8.2.9 #141137。目录正成为主要分发渠道；预计会发布准入文档，并继续按 SHA 锁定进行层级审查。
  3. 网关启动韧性 — #144181 及其修复 #144198：让 stay_alive 在全部三条致命路径上具有权威性。改动小、范围明确，很可能落地。
  4. 将成本/延迟降低作为一项特性 — PR #144177（一次性运行每次调用减少 1,570 个提示 token，每个会话减少 302 个）和 PR #144174（技能索引瘦身）表明维护者正在主动精简系统提示词。提示词效率正被视为一流的路线图事项。

概率较低 / 需要设计：

  • #18964 Reticulum/LXMF 网关 — 受众小，176 天内无维护者表态；走插件/连接器路线比核心支持更有可能。
  • #98004 Bot Mode 的按组自动继续预算 — 明确排在 #89545 之后，但属于 P3 且已闲置 2 个月。
  • PR #144207 terminal.process_priority: low（移植自 OpenHands）和 PR #144211 可续传的模型/工具下载 — 两者都小、可选、低风险；是快速落地的好候选。
  • 在 #134556（pre_send_message）和 #144071（插件人工输入回复）双双关闭后，扩展面方向不明。集成方短期内不应指望出站重写或跨前端审批路由。

7. 用户反馈摘要

真实痛点，归类如下：

  • “我看不出我的 agent 在干什么。” 多会话桌面端用户会丢失后台工作的线索——这是互动量最高的问题。用户想要操作系统级的提示（徽标、未读红点），而不只是应用内状态。
  • “我升级不了。” 持有大体积 state.db 的长期用户在结构上被“立即更新”拒之门外（#133253）；Windows 用户报告在官方 hermes update 之后安装变得*“又不可用了”（#144165）。这类反馈会*侵蚀信任，因为它阻断了对修复的获取。
  • Windows 在实践中是二等平台。 租约泄漏（1,546 个文件）、缺少重启标记、cron 文件共享竞争，以及桌面端启动恢复阻塞——在同一个时间窗口内出现了四种不同的 Windows 独有故障。
  • 多 profile 网关运维者触及扩展上限。 DM 会话无界增长（#136012）、关机刷写不可恢复（#136189）以及看板重复副作用（#144200），描述的都是服务大量 profile/任务的生产网关，其中正确性在无声退化。
  • 澄清/审批流程在重连时不可靠。 用户丢失已锁定的答案，并看到虚假的 undelivered 结果（#144158、#144159）——对会进入后台的移动客户端尤其代价高昂。
  • 插件开发者面临接入摩擦。 一位维护者找不到目录准入途径（#143053）；另一位被 Python 3.14 依赖解析失败阻塞（#144003）；第三位的语音插件卡在等待认证策略审查（#143585）。
  • 桌面端在 Linux/NVIDIA 上资源占用高。 悬停设置按钮会导致 GPU 利用率飙升（#144168）。

满意信号： 报告的质量异常高（二分定位的 SHA、诸如“331 次唤醒运行中 19 次失败”的生产指标、39 次重复的日志证据），用户还主动表达感谢并提供详细复现——善意浓厚、调查投入很高。不满集中在更新路径的可靠性和平台特定故障上，而非核心 agent 能力。

  1. #8891 — [Tracker] 持久内存：将策展、相关性和可操作性平面接通至对等水平 — 12 条评论，自 2026-07-09 开放。 该项目中讨论量最高的条目。一个明确标注的路线图/史诗跟踪器，协调多 PR 分批落地；2026-08-29 的实时快照列出 7 个未完成项（4 个 issue，3 个 PR）。潜在需求： 用户希望跨会话内存达到成熟同类运行时水平——这是 ZeroClaw 感知到的最大能力缺口，也是持续时间最长的协调负担。

  2. #10066 — SOP 引擎排序缺陷 — 5 条评论，现已关闭。 对一个 P0 正确性 issue 参与度高；讨论集中在运行状态完整性，以及验证拒绝与步骤推进如何交错。

  3. #10797 — Markdown 内存后端在重叠 store() 时丢失条目 — 3 条评论，仍开放。 由 agent 上报的路径提交；S0 严重级别。潜在需求： 为最简单、采用最广的内存后端提供持久性保证。

  4. #9592 — 路由更新后的 provider 别名探测 — 3 条评论，已关闭。

  5. #12014、#12005、#11799、#11992、#11853 — 各有 2 条评论。

信号： 社区注意力集中在内存正确性和provider/配置保真度，而非新的通道集成。贡献者 mov-xound-glitch 非常高产（本时间窗口内 5 个 issue + 4 个 PR），JordanTheJet 则主导 SOP/完整性及带发布标签的工作流。

5. 缺陷与稳定性

按严重级别排序：

S0 — 数据丢失

  • #10797 [开放] — MarkdownMemory::store 会从陈旧快照重写文件；没有任何机制串行化并发写入者或验证写入已落盘。重叠的 store() 调用会静默丢失条目。已开放 6 周，本窗口内无关联修复 PR——最高优先级缺口。 相关开放 PR #11663 涉及内存冲突处理，但不涉及此写入路径。

S1 — 工作流受阻

  • #12014 [开放] — 自定义 OpenAI 兼容 provider 在缺少 context_window 时硬回退到 32,000 tokens（CompatibilityFallback），随后在本地拒绝有效轮次。报告并更新于 2026-10-24。已有修复 PR：#12017——"将上下文窗口视为模型元数据，而非配置。" 下一版本的有力候选。
  • #12005 [开放] — PowerShell 方言解析器拒绝任何包含裸 @ 的命令，导致一个已加入允许列表的邮件 CLI 不可用。作为 zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs 中的回归提交，影响 Windows x86_64 上的 v0.8.6。无关联修复 PR。
  • #12009 [已关闭] — 两个 RUSTSEC 公告（发布于 2026-10-23）导致每次 master 构建上的 cargo deny check 失败。一天内解决。

安全 / 供应链

  • #11932 [已关闭] — 已不受信任的 emSign 中间证书仍保留在已发布的容器 CA bundle 中；仅修补 Rust 验证器并不足够。
  • #11853 [开放] — 自动化 npm audit 失败（high/critical：1）影响 @tailwindcss/typography 等；自 2026-10-19 开放，由 bot 提交，2 条评论。用户影响低，但构成反复出现的 CI 噪音。

S3 — 次要

  • #12006 [开放] — tool_search 从注册表构建时的副本提供延迟工具 schema，因此由实时配置驱动的 schema 在重载后变得陈旧。修复 PR：#12007。
  • #11792 [开放] — 中断的 plugin install 可能留下孤立的 .<name>.installing-v1-<id> 暂存目录，且没有任何命令回收（磁盘泄漏）。标记为 release:v0.9.0。
  • #11946 / #11945 [开放] — 来自 #11861 的后续事项：陈旧的确定性 SOP 检查点副本不得覆盖所有者的 {run}.state.json，另缺少这些分支的测试覆盖。

已关闭的稳定性成果： #11899（网关重载后连接/配置代际泄漏）与 #10066（SOP schema 拒绝排序）都代表对长生命周期运行有意义的完整性改进。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

本窗口内明确的用户请求：

请求 Issue 近期交付可能性
Shell 策略拒绝应指明拒绝规则并接受操作员提示 #11799 中等——小型、范围明确、贴近安全的 DX 修复
send_via 显式 attachments 在读取策略下检查 #11996 高——实现已作为 PR #11997 开放
电子邮件通道：操作员模板 + 净化后的 HTML 正文 #11992 中等——与 #11997 自然配套
嵌入二进制为聊天/cron 轮次添加钩子 #12016 已关闭（2026-10-24）
无 SMTP 的仅入站电子邮件通道 PR #12003 评审中——降低只读邮箱访问门槛

路线图信号：

  • Goal Mode V1 正以 12 部分提案系列分阶段推进；#11879 是“提案 2/12”，并且刻意保持休眠（仅配置 + 命令语法，无可执行行为）。预计 Goal Mode 将跨多个版本落地，而非在 v0.8.7 中。
  • 会话事件历史（#11921，size:XL）提出仅追加的规范会话事件，以实现副作用安全重放——这是架构变更，而非单点功能。
  • 持久内存对等（#8891）仍是路线图的首要承诺。
  • 消息广度：带可选 OMEMO 的 XMPP/Prosody（#11847）表明对自托管/联邦传输的持续需求。

预测： v0.8.7 将随上述 SOP/网关/安全修复发布，且很可能不含新功能。v0.9.0 范围正围绕插件安装健壮性（#11792）、send_via 附件（#11997）、上下文窗口语义（#12017）以及持续的内存工作（#11663、#8891）收敛。

7. 用户反馈摘要

痛点，按证据强度排序：

  1. 内存尚不可信。 参与度最高的跟踪器（#8891，12 条评论，已 3.5 个月）加上 S0 并发写入数据丢失缺陷（#10797）以及 supersession 评分缺陷（#11663——BM25 归一化可能给无关行赋予 1.0，导致整合时将其软隐藏）都指向同一个未满足需求：可靠、非破坏性的长期召回。
  2. 平台/区域设置边缘情况影响严重。 PowerShell @ 回归（#12005）使整个已加入允许列表的工作流在 Windows 上不可用——这是安全加固破坏合法操作员的案例。类似地，provider 配置缺口会静默退化为本地拒绝的轮次（#12014）。
  3. 不透明的安全拒绝令操作员沮丧。 #11799 明确要求说明命令为何被拒绝，并提供可由操作员配置的提示。这是对安全层可用性的抱怨，而非要求削弱它。
  4. 电子邮件仍是二等公民。 自 #9993 起，发送侧完全无法附加文件（#11996），而仅入站邮箱甚至无法表达（#12003）。用户正推动电子邮件达到生产级对等。
  5. 问题归因/响应速度是一个积极信号。 #12016 在 24 小时内关闭；#12009（破坏 CI 的公告）在提交当天关闭；#10066 与 #11932（均为高风险）今日关闭。本窗口内的不满来自能力缺口，而非维护者忽视。

数据中可见的使用场景： 将 ZeroClaw 作为库嵌入更大的二进制（钩子，#12016）；使用邮件 CLI 的 Windows 原生 shell 自动化；具有非常规上下文大小的 OpenAI 兼容自托管/第三方端点；只读合规邮箱；通过 XMPP 的联邦聊天。

8. 待办积压观察

需要维护者关注的事项，按风险 × 陈旧度排序：

事项 存在时长 为何重要
#8891 — 持久内存对等跟踪器 约 3.5 个月（创建于 2026-07-09） 参与度最高的条目；快照日期为 2026-08-29，现已陈旧约 8 周。需要刷新状态表。
#10797 — Markdown 后端数据丢失（S0） 约 6 周（2026-09-12） S0 且无关联修复 PR。数据集中持续时间最长的严重开放缺陷。
#9420 — Anthropic 存储的 OAuth 配置档案 约 3 个月（2026-07-26） Size:XL、risk:high、trusted contributor；触及 core/provider/gateway 与安全域。高价值、高评审成本——很可能缺乏评审者带宽。
#10446 — 拒绝泄漏进普通文本的工具调用信封 约 2 个月（2026-08-29） domain:security、risk:high、size:XL；描述了 gpt-5.6/codex 上间歇性生产发生的情况。据作者称可干净合并——阻塞在评审，而非冲突。
#11422 — TUI 签名绑定到配置拥有的密钥 约 3 周（2026-10-02） size:XL，阻塞于 #11411/#11576；#12013 已从中提取为更小、可测试的切片——这是值得延续的良好解除阻塞模式。
#11853 — npm audit 失败（bot） 6 天 反复出现的自动化安全发现需要分诊/轮换策略，而非一次性修复。
#11792 — 孤立的插件安装暂存目录 9 天 标记为 v0.9.0 且无关联 PR；一个小型、自包含的修复，可清除一类已知磁盘泄漏。

积压健康度结论： 47 个开放 / 3 个关闭的 PR 比例是本摘要中最重要的结构性数字。若干大型、高风险 PR（#9420、#10446、#11422、#11921）在技术上已就绪，但受限于评审，而快速收益（#12007、#12013、#11997）则在推进。瓶颈是对 XL/risk:high 变更的评审能力，而非贡献者供给。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-25

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-25 00:29 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-25

Data note: the supplied dataset covers 500 issues and 500 PRs updated in the last 24 hours. PR comment counts were not populated, so PR rankings below use labels, status, and stated impact rather than comment volume.

1. Today’s Overview

OpenClaw remains a very high-velocity project: 500 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24 hours, with 92 issues closed and 259 PRs merged or closed. Two releases shipped — a patch release focused on replay-safe session recovery and an extended-stable/LTS gateway release with security and reliability backports. Activity is heavily weighted toward regression and stability work rather than net-new features, especially around plugin source capture, SQLite/state management, session recovery, and Windows update flows. Project health is mixed: maintainer throughput is strong and an LTS channel exists, but several P0/P1 regressions remain open, including the highest-comment issue in the dataset. The volume of stale and needs-maintainer-review labels suggests review bandwidth, not contributor interest, is the main bottleneck.

2. Releases

v2026.10.7

  • Focus: Replay-safe session recovery.
  • Noted changes:
    • Interrupted sessions retain recovery provenance and unfinished tool outcomes.
    • Stopped conversations retire terminal recovery residue before accepting the next message.
    • Rejected Claude CLI drafts are kept out of final replies.
    • Additional large-change notes are truncated in the supplied data.
  • Breaking changes / migration: No explicit breaking changes or migration steps were provided in the excerpt. Given the session-state and recovery changes, operators should validate interrupted-session and tool-outcome behavior after upgrade.
  • Link: OpenClaw releases

v2026.9.34

  • Channel: Gateway-only extended-stable, described as the current LTS equivalent.
  • Contents: OpenClaw from the end of September 2026 plus critical security updates, reliability and performance fixes, and new model support.
  • Recommendation: Appropriate for production/LTS users who prioritize stability over the 2026.10 feature line.
  • Link: OpenClaw releases

Beta signal: PR #182951 references v2026.10.10-beta.3, indicating an active beta channel beyond the latest stable release listed here.

3. Project Progress

With 259 PRs merged or closed in the last 24 hours, progress was concentrated in reliability, performance, and UI collaboration:

  • Session/state performance: #182934 (closed) shared resident actor entries across projections, reducing duplicate decoded session entries.
  • Mention/Inbox architecture: #155419 (closed) moved Inbox database work off the Gateway thread; #153812 (closed) added session mention notifications in the UI.
  • Packaging/update reliability: #182982 (closed) restored standalone helper launches for update, MCP, and file-transfer helpers after packaging.
  • CLI stall fix: #182984 (closed) avoided minutes-long SQLite integrity_check scans when a CLI opens an agent database already held by the Gateway.
  • Open P0 fix: #182951 routes config set/patch/unset through a running Gateway, fixing an exit-1 regression in v2026.10.10-beta.3.
  • Performance PR queue: #183034 reduces transcript turn DB round trips; #183042 defers dormant Chat work during cold boot; #182976 reuses validated entry facts for cold history accounting.
  • Channel reliability: #183028 fixes Telegram ask_user questions being dropped during progress-draft retirement.
  • Provider/runtime: #176567 fixes OpenAI realtime voice sockets bypassing the managed proxy on Bun; #180599 keeps Code Mode run expiry on the monotonic clock.

Theme: The merged/open PR set shows a clear push toward reducing database round trips, improving cold-start UI behavior, and hardening session/mention delivery. Feature work is secondary to stabilizing the 2026.9/2026.10 regressions.

4. Community Hot Topics

Most active issues

  1. #160959 — P0: Gateway blocks for minutes while capturing large external plugins — 50 comments, crash-loop, no-new-fix-pr.

    • Since plugin generation capture landed in 2026.9.6, a Gateway with a large external/workspace plugin blocks its event loop for minutes at startup and when the prepared model runtime republishes.
    • Underlying need: Plugin capture must be asynchronous/bounded, with reuse and native-binary handling. This is the clearest subsystem-level regression in the dataset.

  2. #164294 — P2: Gateway state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes — 30 comments.

    • WAL checkpoint is permanently blocked by an in-process reader; checkpointedFrames=866 vs logFrames=17091.
    • Underlying need: SQLite reader lifecycle management and observable checkpoint diagnostics.

  3. #159356 — P2: llama.cpp manager reports ready while embedding child exits — 29 comments.

    • Embedding requests return HTTP 500 after the child process exits; memory pressure is suspected but not confirmed.
    • Underlying need: process supervision and readiness semantics for local model children.

  4. #157989 — P1: Plugin source capture rewrites 1.1–1.4 GB per CLI command and ~6.5 GB per Gateway start — 23 comments.

    • Severe SSD wear from repeated byte-copying and SHA-256 hashing of external plugins.
    • Underlying need: capture caching/reuse and exclusion of bundled native binaries.

  5. #53408 — P2: Write/exec tool parameters silently dropped after long conversations — 15 comments, 2 👍, stale since March 2026.

    • After 15+ turns with heavy tool use, write and exec arrive with empty argument objects.
    • Underlying need: long-session tool-call serialization integrity — a long-standing trust issue.

Active PRs worth watching

  • #182951 — P0: Route config mutations through a running Gateway
  • #176567 — P1: OpenAI realtime voice proxy on Bun
  • #182066 — perf(cron): reuse source validation at transcript target checks — ready for maintainer look
  • #183034 — improve(sessions): reduce transcript turn DB round trips

Analysis: Three of the top four issues (#160959, #157989, #162585) share the same plugin source-capture root cause. SQLite/state DB lifecycle issues form a second cluster (#164294, #164948, #175926, #181660). The community is disproportionately affected by a small number of subsystems, which makes targeted fixes high-leverage.

5. Bugs & Stability

P0 / release-blocking

  • #160959 — OPEN. Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins; crash-loop; 50 comments. No fix PR tagged.
  • #181660 — CLOSED. SQLite “Session read batch cannot reenter an active SQLite writer admission” on 2026.10.6; P0 UX release blocker.
  • #153426 — OPEN. Curated MEMORY.md/USER.md roots silently and permanently excluded from bootstrap injection by the provenance ratchet; security/session-state; P0.
  • #166634 — OPEN. Late reclamation checkpoint failure leaves agent unavailable after crash recovery; P0.
  • #182951 — OPEN PR. Config mutations fail with exclusive-offline-state error whenever a Gateway is running; regression in v2026.10.10-beta.3; P0 fix PR open.

P1

  • #157989 — OPEN. Plugin capture SSD wear; no fix PR.
  • #181619 — CLOSED. Codex app-server execution-budget timeout regression after 2026.10.5 → 2026.10.6; every primary turn failed and fell back silently.
  • #135858 — CLOSED. opencode-go local catalog snapshot did not project provider.npm→api override; broke muse-spark-1.2-contributor and omitted mimo-v2.5.
  • #182476 — OPEN. Windows update repair fails with OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST; gateway readiness slow/unstable.
  • #150822 — OPEN. Native Codex children advertise OpenClaw tools without an execution handler; detached failure delivery also fails; security-sensitive.
  • #154299 — OPEN. Subagent completion-delivery final text silently drops on 2026.9.5; no queue entry or failure record.
  • #167876 — OPEN. Talk consultations lose caller authority after session setup; security/other.
  • #148292 — OPEN. Session auto-compaction single attempt with no timeout; 23-minute hangs.
  • #158154 — OPEN. Telegram subagent result announcements expire undelivered after 30 minutes; retries stall topic lanes for hours.
  • #178300 — OPEN. Settled-turn finalization after a 1-token length stop delivers false success.
  • #178000 — CLOSED. Session-state races trigger cross-provider model fallback as reason=unknown.

P2 clusters

  • Plugin capture / Windows: #162585 (staging re-materializes plugin into itself, 290 MB → 612 MB+/24 min), #157812 (Windows auto-update failure modes).
  • SQLite/state: #164294 (WAL checkpoint), #164948 (doctor --fix self-deadlock, busyTimeoutMs=0), #175926 (snapshot reclamation skips every cycle).
  • Session/tool integrity: #159789 (one failed native close permanently locks agent execution), #157986 (Automations agentTurn DataCloneError), #146902 (tool-set churn defeats prompt-cache reuse).
  • UI/UX: #164394 (WebChat transcript jitter), #149912 (text rendered twice/thrice), #165041 (internal context injection visible), #137188 (stale progress card live spinner).
  • Provider/cache/cost: #161208 (heartbeats never reuse Anthropic prompt cache; ~$0.40–0.95 per heartbeat), #162768 (Codex model discovery hardcodes client_version=0.158.0), #144797 (reused claude-cli session keeps deleted --mcp-config, tools die with 401).
  • Security: #158966 (credentialed CDP WebSocket URLs reach model-facing tab results).
  • Platform: #154104 (idle Matrix E2EE ~50% CPU, ~52 MB/min writes), #153622 (macOS Peekaboo transient UUID snapshot).

Fix PRs in flight: #183052 (agent DB integrity check), #183002 (monotonic clock across clock jumps), #183028 (Telegram questions), #180850 (doctor malformed UTF-8), #183000 (PostgreSQL config reporting), #183015 (PostgreSQL limited ordered reads). The top P0 issue #160959 still lacks a fix PR.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #182712 — Limit-aware model fallback (P2, 7 comments): skip candidates in an exhausted provider quota pool and prefer a different provider. Strong candidate for near-term model-routing work.
  • #155633 — Add Databricks Unity Gateway as an official model provider (P2): implementation PR #155634 exists. Enterprise provider expansion is likely.
  • #139477 — Honor tools.toolSearch for bundle-MCP CLI backends (P2, diamond lobster): loopback MCP config hardcodes alwaysLoad: true, eagerly expanding every tool schema. Directly relevant to prompt/token efficiency.
  • #150598 — Completion-wake delivery semantics (P2): field-data proposal for terminal-only, new-turn, coalesced, and failure-as-triage delivery in multi-session orchestration.
  • #141004 — Record observed runtime skill usage (open PR since Sept 7): durable audit surface for skill reads/invocations.
  • #137613 — Pre-compaction memory flush on CLI backends (P2, diamond lobster): memory flush is gated off for claude-cli, so CLI-backed sessions lose durable notes before compaction.
  • #96675 — Owner-signed responsibility gates for memory, actions, skills, evidence reuse (closed enhancement): signals continued demand for explicit user confirmation before persistent memory/action reuse.
  • #153812 — Show session mention notifications (closed): UI collaboration feature likely to appear in a near-term release.

Prediction: The next release likely emphasizes session recovery/provenance refinements, config routing through a running Gateway, plugin-capture performance, limit-aware model fallback, and mention/Telegram delivery reliability. New model support is already flowing through the extended-stable channel.

7. User Feedback Summary

Main pain points

  • Operational cost and hardware wear: Plugin source capture causes GB-scale writes per command and per Gateway start (#157989, #162585). Matrix E2EE idles at ~50% CPU and ~52 MB/min writes (#154104).
  • Update/install fragility on Windows: Repeated auto-update failures, unexpanded $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, abandoned update records, and lease loss during repair (#157812, #182476).
  • Session reliability and message loss: Agent execution locks after a failed native close (#159789); subagent final text drops (#154299); Telegram announcements expire (#158154); crash recovery can leave an agent unavailable (#166634).
  • Trust/security concerns: Curated memory files can be silently excluded forever (#153426); credentialed CDP URLs reach model-facing output (#158966); Talk calls lose caller authority (#167876).
  • Cost visibility: Heartbeats never reuse Anthropic prompt cache, costing roughly $0.40–0.95 each (#161208).
  • UI polish: WebChat transcript jitter (#164394), duplicate/thrice rendering (#149912), visible internal context injection (#165041), stale progress spinners (#137188).

Use cases represented

  • Heavy multi-session orchestration with subagents, long-running background jobs, and coordinator sessions.
  • Telegram, Matrix, and QQ channel deployments, including forum topics and E2EE.
  • CLI-backed models (claude-cli, Codex app-server) and local embedding stacks (llama.cpp).
  • Windows desktop/server installs and npm global deployments.
  • Large external plugin trees with native binaries.

Satisfaction/dissatisfaction: Users are providing detailed, high-quality reproductions and operational workarounds, which indicates strong engagement. Dissatisfaction is concentrated in regressions introduced during the 2026.9.x line, Windows update reliability, and long-lived stale issues. The extended-stable/LTS release is a positive signal for production users.

8. Backlog Watch

These items are important but have gone long without resolution or clear maintainer ownership:

  • #53408 — Write/exec parameters silently dropped after long conversations — opened 2026-03-24; 15 comments, 2 👍; stale. The oldest high-impact tool-integrity issue in the dataset.
  • #141172 — Run dies before first session commit leaks agent.run.started forever — opened 2026-09-07; stale; trajectory flush FK failures and missing agent.run.finished.
  • #137613 — Pre-compaction memory flush disabled on CLI backends — opened 2026-09-03; diamond lobster; 10 comments; durable-memory loss risk.
  • #146902 — Same-session tool-set churn defeats prompt-cache reuse — opened 2026-09-13; 11 comments; direct cost/performance impact.
  • #149631 — PR preflight throws at 121 jobs against 120 Node matrix cap — opened 2026-09-16; CI gate fails before tests start.
  • #150598 — Completion-wake delivery semantics proposal — opened 2026-09-17; product-decision needed.
  • #148292 — Auto-compaction 23-minute hangs — opened 2026-09-14; P1; session-state.
  • #154104 — Idle Matrix E2EE ~50% CPU and ~52 MB/min writes — opened 2026-09-20; operational cost.
  • #145937 — QQ channel left without a fully working plugin on 2026.9.x — opened 2026-09-12; first-party plugin crashes on inbound; successor receives zero chunks.
  • #144976 — Gateway auto-restarts after slow explicit stop on systemd — opened 2026-09-11; lifecycle correctness.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent OSS Ecosystem

Window: 2026-10-25 community digests. Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw.
Health score: analyst composite (0–10) weighting release cadence, issue/PR throughput, regression/security burden, review backlog, and process maturity. Not a formal benchmark.

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent OSS landscape is entering a reliability-and-governance phase: projects are shipping fewer net-new capabilities and spending more effort on session recovery, state-store lifecycle, plugin governance, delivery guarantees, and upgrade safety. OpenClaw remains the scale leader with a gateway-centric architecture and an LTS channel, while Hermes Agent, ZeroClaw, and QwenPaw occupy narrower but credible positions around desktop sessions, SOP/security workflows, and multi-agent governance respectively. Across projects, community feedback is dominated by silent failures, data durability, plugin/extension trust, platform-specific update breakage, and cost/latency visibility. IronClaw is inactive in this window. The strongest differentiator is no longer model access; it is operational trust — whether sessions, memory, plugins, channels, and upgrades behave predictably under production load.

3. OpenClaw’s Position

Advantages vs peers

  • Scale and throughput: 1,000 updated issues/PRs in 24h, 259 PRs merged/closed, and 92 issues closed. This is an order of magnitude above Hermes and ZeroClaw and far above QwenPaw.
  • Release maturity: Only project with a visible stable + LTS/extended-stable process and an active beta line. Hermes and QwenPaw shipped nothing; ZeroClaw’s v0.8.7 is prepared but unpublished.
  • Breadth: Gateway, providers, plugins, channels, session recovery, Windows update flows, SQLite state management, local embeddings, and command-line tooling all active in one ecosystem.
  • Ecosystem gravity: Large external plugin trees, multi-session orchestration, Telegram/Matrix/QQ deployments, CLI-backed models, and Windows/npm installs are all represented in feedback.

Weaknesses vs peers

  • Regression debt: P0 plugin source-capture blockage (#160959, 50 comments) and P1 SSD-wear capture (#157989) are high-leverage unresolved clusters; #160959 has no fix PR.
  • Review bandwidth: stale and needs-maintainer-review labels indicate review capacity, not contributor interest, is the bottleneck.
  • SQLite/state and Windows update fragility: Several P0/P1 issues remain around WAL checkpointing, reader lifecycle, crash recovery, and OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST.

Technical approach differences

  • OpenClaw is gateway-centric: a long-running Gateway owns config, sessions, state DB, plugin capture, and channel routing. Recent work routes config mutations through a running Gateway and improves replay-safe session recovery.
  • Peers are more narrowly scoped: Hermes is Desktop/session-lifecycle-heavy; ZeroClaw is Rust/Tauri with SOP, policy, and memory backends; QwenPaw is governance/audit and multi-agent orchestration-heavy.
  • OpenClaw’s LTS channel gives it a production-adoption advantage that no peer currently matches in this dataset.

Update/install reliability is a trust gate Hermes state.db preflight blocks update; OpenClaw Windows lease/update failures; Windows regressions in both Test upgrades with realistic user data volumes and platform-specific installers; make update paths atomic and resumable.
Channel delivery is becoming product-critical Telegram expiration, Bot Chat title collisions, Matrix E2EE recovery, QQ streaming, email attachments, XMPP Abstract transport with explicit delivery semantics: retry, reconnect, dedupe, attachment parity, and terminal-state acknowledgement.
Cost/latency optimization is moving into core OpenClaw prompt-cache misses and heartbeat cost; Hermes prompt trimming; ZeroClaw context-window metadata fallback Build cache-aware prompt assembly, model metadata normalization, limit-aware fallback, and token/cost observability into routing.

Bottom line: OpenClaw is the ecosystem’s scale and release-process leader, but its next quality step depends on resolving the plugin-capture and SQLite/state clusters. Hermes and ZeroClaw are credible Tier-2 projects with strong user engagement but review-bound roadmaps and unresolved foundational design questions. QwenPaw has serious production users but must improve merge throughput and silent-failure observability. Across all active projects, the winning agent platforms will be those that make sessions, memory, plugins, channels, and upgrades observable, recoverable, and trustworthy — not merely feature-rich.

Issue #136189 — P1: shutdown flush files written under the wrong session key (4 comments) Messages queued at shutdown are keyed by adapter isolation flags while recovery resolves them via gateway-wide flags, so restart recovery can never map them when the flags differ. 7. User Feedback Summary

Real pain points, grouped:

  • "I can't tell what my agent is doing." Multi-session Desktop users lose track of backgrounded work — the top issue by engagement. Users want OS-level affordances (badges, unread dots), not just in-app state.
  • "I can't upgrade." Long-term users with large state.db files are structurally locked out of "Update now" (#133253); Windows users report the install becoming "unusable again" after an official hermes update (#144165). This is a trust-eroding class of feedback because it blocks access to fixes.
  • Windows is a second-class platform in practice. Lease leakage (1,546 files), missing restart markers, cron file-sharing races, and Desktop startup recovery blocking are four distinct Windows-only failures in one window.
  • Multi-profile gateway operators hit scaling limits. Unbounded DM sessions (#136012), unrecoverable shutdown flush (#136189), and duplicate kanban side effects (#144200) all describe production gateways serving many profiles/jobs where correctness degrades silently.
  • Clarify/approval flows are unreliable across reconnects. Users lose locked answers and see spurious undelivered outcomes (#144158, #144159) — particularly costly for mobile clients that background.
  • Plugin developers face onboarding friction. One maintainer cannot find the catalog admission route (#143053); another is blocked by a Python 3.14 dependency resolution failure (#144003); a third's voice plugin is stuck pending authentication-policy review (#143585).
  • Desktop is heavy on Linux/NVIDIA. Hovering Settings buttons spikes GPU utilization (#144168).

Satisfaction signals: Reports are unusually well-engineered (bisected SHAs, production metrics like "19 failures out of 331 wake-runs," 39-repetition log evidence), and users volunteer thanks and detailed repros — high goodwill and high investigative effort. Dissatisfaction concentrates on reliability of the update path and on platform-specific breakage, not on core agent capability.

Issue #8252 — 4 comments, [CLOSED] [Bug] — Agent-to-agent (ChatWithAgent) sessions silently cancelled with CancelledError; cancellations occur in same-second pairs, produce zero artifacts, and record neither the initiating party nor the reason. Reporter runs a multi-agent fleet (Orchestrator / Reasoner / Executor / Reviewer / Defender) behind a Feishu channel entry, and cites qwenpaw/hooks/error/error_hook.py:90 and qwenpaw/runtime/run.... Underlying need: multi-agent orchestration users need cancellation to be attributable — who cancelled, why, and what was lost — otherwise fleet debugging is intractable.
  2. Issue #8406 — 2 comments, [OPEN] [Bug] — QQ channel enabled flag silently reset to false with no warning. Underlying need: configuration must be authoritative and any mutation must be logged; silent config rollback breaks trust in long-running deployments. (Data-quality note: the issue body renders as an unexpanded template placeholder $(cat /tmp/issue_body.md), limiting triage.)
  3. Issue #8412 — 1 comment, [OPEN] [Bug] — governance/audit.db (audit_events) stops recording per-agent tool calls despite audit_level: all in each governance/<agent>_<hash>/policy.yaml; once rows stop, they never resume while the agent keeps calling tools, including file writes.
  4. Issue #8407 — 1 comment, [OPEN] [Feature] — Requests a server-side default for the Console "assistant message display mode" (currently only localStorage key qwenpaw_assistant_message_display_mode).

Signal: the top three threads all describe state changing or failing silently. This is the dominant community concern this cycle.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

Severity Item Status
Critical #8252 — Agent-to-agent sessions silently cancelled; artifacts zeroed; no initiator/reason recorded. Affects core multi-agent orchestration and produces total work loss. CLOSED, but no linked fix PR in this dataset — closure reason unverified; root cause may be unaddressed.
High #8412 — Per-agent audit logging permanently stops despite audit_level: all. A governance/compliance control failing open-but-silent is arguably worse than failing loudly; file-write tool calls go unlogged. OPEN, no fix PR.
High #7835 — Auto-memory-recall injects a synthetic ToolCallBlock + ToolResultBlock pair into LLM context; Console hides it via MemorySearchCard, but every other outbound channel (Feishu, etc.) leaks it. Privacy/UX leak. OPEN, Under Review since 2026-09-17.
Medium #8406 — QQ channel enabled flag silently reset to false; no warning surfaced. Silent config regression. OPEN, no fix PR.
Medium #8411 / #8365 — Matrix cached-session and missing-device-key recovery; health check reports healthy channel while E2EE keys are never re-uploaded. False-positive health signal. PR closed without merge — regression risk persists.
Medium #7211 — HookContext.inject_context() payload persists as a user turn / searchable history instead of staying request-local. Context pollution and history contamination. OPEN, ready-for-human-review since 2026-08-21.

Fix-PR coverage: 1 of 6 has an associated fix PR (#8411, closed unmerged). Five have none.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Team/self-hosted configurable defaults — #8407 asks to move the assistant message display mode from browser localStorage to server-provided defaults, matching the existing /config/theme pattern (chat_display.assistant_message_display_mode). Already paired with an implementation: #8408 size/M. Small, self-contained, follows an established pattern → high likelihood for the next release.
  • QQ C2C streaming — #8409 size/L implements on_streaming_start/delta/end via POST /v2/users/{user_openid}/stream_messages, gated behind streaming_enabled (QQ_STREAMING_ENABLED). Closes feature request #8307. Channel-parity work; plausible next-cycle candidate if review capacity exists.
  • Model pool lifecycle — #8410 size/M adds a Remove action (with confirmation) for provider-managed entries, fixing #8195. Low risk; likely to land early.
  • Memory subsystem upgrade — #8347 size/XXXL bumps ReMe 0.4.1.11 → 0.4.2.0, adapts background indexing / Auto-Dream consolidation, and adds opt-in, default-off decision compaction, conversation image memory, and entity tagging. All new behavior is default-off → low user-facing risk, but the PR size itself is a review bottleneck. Realistic for a minor/larger release, not the next patch.

Prediction: next patch likely ships #8408 + #8410, possibly the three trivial docs-anchor PRs (#8401–#8403); #8409 and #8347 are more likely to slip a cycle.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Deployment profiles are serious and production-like: multi-agent fleets with role separation (Orchestrator/Reasoner/Executor/Reviewer/Defender), Feishu/Lark entry channels, QQ channels, password-authenticated Matrix homeservers, and self-hosted team deployments with admin-managed policy files. This is not hobbyist usage.
  • Primary pain point — silent failure: three of four issues use "silently" or describe state that changes/stops with no warning (#8252 cancel with no initiator/reason, #8406 flag reset, #8412 audit logging dead). Users are not asking for features; they are asking to be told when something goes wrong.
  • Auditability and governance are load-bearing: policy.yaml + governance/audit.db are used as compliance controls per agent; their silent failure undermines the trust model of the whole governance layer.
  • Multi-device / team ergonomics: Console preferences tied to localStorage are described as lost on cache clear or new device, and admins cannot set defaults for members — a concrete self-hosting friction point.
  • Satisfaction signal: reports are detailed, reproduced with versions and file/line references, and accompanied by community PRs (#8408 author also filed #8407). That indicates engaged users investing in the project — but also that maintainer responsiveness on silent-failure bugs is the main satisfaction risk.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or high-importance items needing maintainer attention:

  1. PR #7211 — first-time-contributor, ready-for-human-review, size/L, open since 2026-08-21 (~9 weeks). Fixes injected context persisting into conversation history (#6360, #6358). A first-time contributor sitting 2+ months in ready-for-human-review is a community-retention risk.
  2. PR #7390 — size/XS test-only regression guard for Aliyun Coding Plan catalog drift (#6551), open since 2026-08-28 (~8 weeks). Trivial size, clear value, still unmerged — a review-queue anomaly worth escalating.
  3. PR #7835 — Under Review since 2026-09-17 (~5 weeks). Fixes a genuine cross-channel privacy leak (memory-recall trace escaping to Feishu and other channels). Should be prioritized on privacy grounds.
  4. PR #8347 — size/XXXL ReMe upgrade. Needs maintainer review bandwidth plus coordination with ReMe #672; high merge-conflict risk the longer it sits.
  5. Issue #8252 — closed without a linked fix PR in this dataset. Closed-but-unresolved critical orchestration bug; recommend a maintainer post-closure note confirming fix version or root cause.
  6. Issue #8412 — governance audit DB silently dying is a compliance-class defect with zero fix PRs; recommend a triage label and owner within this cycle.
  7. Issue #8406 — body still contains an unexpanded $(cat /tmp/issue_body.md) placeholder; needs a request-for-repro before it can be actioned.

Digest compiled from 4 issues and 11 pull requests updated in the 24h window ending 2026-10-24. PR comment counts and 👍 totals were unavailable (undefined) in the source data and are excluded from rankings.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-25

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw is in a release-stabilization phase: six issues were closed in the last 24 hours, including a P0 SOP-engine correctness bug and two high-risk security items, and PR #12011 (chore(release): bump version to v0.8.7) has closed out, with several bugs explicitly tagged release:v0.8.7. Activity volume is high — 18 issues and 50 PRs touched — but the shape is lopsided: 47 of 50 updated PRs remain open versus only 3 merged/closed, indicating a widening review backlog rather than a merge-heavy sprint. No GitHub release has been published yet, so the v0.8.7 bump is prepared but not shipped. Quality signals are mixed-positive: strong security responsiveness (RUSTSEC advisories closed same-day) alongside persistent S0 data-loss exposure in the memory subsystem (#10797) that has been open 6 weeks.

Data note: the PR feed reports Comments: undefined for all items, so PR comment counts cannot be ranked. Community Hot Topics below ranks by issue comment count and label weight.

2. Releases

No new releases published in the last 24 hours.

However, a release is clearly imminent:

  • PR #12011 [CLOSED] — chore(release): bump version to v0.8.7 — coordinated workspace bump 0.8.6 → 0.8.7 across Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock (30 workspace packages), Tauri config, setup.bat, and crates.io/Discord metadata. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12011
  • Issues tagged release:v0.8.7 and closed today: #10066 (SOP schema-rejection ordering), #11899 (gateway serving stale connections after reload), #12009 (RUSTSEC-2026-0385 / -0386 blocking the Security job).

Predicted v0.8.7 contents: SOP run-integrity fixes, gateway reload lifecycle fix, container CA bundle refresh, and dependency advisory remediation. No breaking changes or migration notes are signaled in the data.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs (3): Only #12011 (version bump) is visible in the top-20 sample; the remaining two merged/closed PRs are not in the supplied slice.

Closed issues — what actually landed or was resolved (6):

Issue Severity Outcome
#10066 — SOP engine promotes later steps before recording output-schema rejection S1, P0 Closed; workflow-blocking ordering bug fixed for v0.8.7
#12009 — cargo deny fails on RUSTSEC-2026-0385 (ctutils) / -0386 (tokio) S1 Closed same-day as report; CI unblocked
#11932 — container CA bundles trust distrusted emSign chains S0 security Closed; native CA bundle corrected
#11899 — stopped gateway keeps serving already-accepted connections after reload Gateway/config lifecycle Closed; config-generation leak after reload addressed
#9592 — provider probe reads pre-update config snapshot S2 Closed; model_routing_config now probes the saved alias
#12016 — let embedding binaries add hooks to chat and cron turns Feature Closed within one day of filing (fast turnaround)

Features advancing in open PRs: session event history (#11921), goal-mode command grammar (#11879, dormant config only), cron-to-conversation binding (#11441), XMPP/OMEMO channel (#11847), inbound-only email (#12003), send_via attachments (#11997), and two RPC/TUI signing-hardening PRs (#11422, #12013).

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment volume (issues only; PR comment data unavailable).

  1. #8891 — [Tracker] Persistent memory: wire curation, relevance, and operability planes to parity — 12 comments, open since 2026-07-09. The single most-discussed item in the project. An explicitly labeled roadmap/epic tracker coordinating a multi-PR rollout; the live snapshot from 2026-08-29 lists 7 open items (4 issues, 3 PRs). Underlying need: users want cross-session memory that matches mature peer runtimes — this is ZeroClaw's largest perceived capability gap and its longest-running coordination burden.

  2. #10066 — SOP engine ordering bug — 5 comments, now closed. High engagement on a P0 correctness issue; the discussion centered on run-state integrity and how validation rejections interleave with step promotion.

  3. #10797 — Markdown memory backend loses entries on overlapping store() — 3 comments, open. Filed by an agent-reported path; S0 severity. Underlying need: durability guarantees for the simplest, most-adopted memory backend.

  4. #9592 — provider alias probe after routing update — 3 comments, closed.

  5. #12014, #12005, #11799, #11992, #11853 — 2 comments each.

Signal: the community's attention is concentrated on memory correctness and provider/config fidelity, not on new channel integrations. Contributor mov-xound-glitch is highly prolific (5 issues + 4 PRs in this window) and JordanTheJet dominates the SOP/integrity and release-tagged workstream.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

S0 — Data loss

  • #10797 [OPEN] — MarkdownMemory::store rewrites the file from a stale snapshot; nothing serializes concurrent writers or verifies the write landed. Overlapping store() calls silently lose entries. Open 6 weeks, no linked fix PR in this window — highest-priority gap. Related open PR #11663 touches memory conflict handling but not this write path.

S1 — Workflow blocked

  • #12014 [OPEN] — Custom OpenAI-compatible provider without context_window hard-falls back to 32,000 tokens (CompatibilityFallback) and then rejects valid turns locally. Reported and updated 2026-10-24. Fix PR exists: #12017 — "treat the context window as model metadata, not configuration." Strong candidate for the next release.
  • #12005 [OPEN] — PowerShell dialect parser rejects any command containing a bare @, making an allowlisted mail CLI unusable. Filed as a regression in zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs, affecting v0.8.6 on Windows x86_64. No linked fix PR.
  • #12009 [CLOSED] — Two RUSTSEC advisories (published 2026-10-23) broke cargo deny check on every master build. Resolved within a day.

Security / supply chain

  • #11932 [CLOSED] — distrusted emSign intermediates remained in published container CA bundles; patching the Rust verifier alone was insufficient.
  • #11853 [OPEN] — automated npm audit failure (high/critical: 1) affecting @tailwindcss/typography and others; open since 2026-10-19, bot-filed, 2 comments. Low user impact but recurring CI noise.

S3 — Minor

  • #12006 [OPEN] — tool_search serves deferred tool schemas from registry-build-time copies, so live-config-driven schemas go stale after reload. Fix PR: #12007.
  • #11792 [OPEN] — an interrupted plugin install can leave an orphaned .<name>.installing-v1-<id> stage directory that no command reclaims (disk leak). Tagged release:v0.9.0.
  • #11946 / #11945 [OPEN] — follow-ups from #11861: a stale deterministic SOP checkpoint copy must not overwrite the owner's {run}.state.json, plus missing test coverage for those branches.

Closed stability wins: #11899 (gateway post-reload connection/config-generation leak) and #10066 (SOP schema-rejection ordering) both represent meaningful integrity improvements to long-lived runs.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Explicit user requests in this window:

Request Issue Likelihood of near-term delivery
Shell policy refusals should name the refusing rule and accept an operator hint #11799 Medium — small, well-scoped, security-adjacent DX fix
send_via explicit attachments checked under read policy #11996 High — implementation already open as PR #11997
Email channel: operator templates + sanitized HTML body #11992 Medium — natural companion to #11997
Embedding binaries add hooks to chat/cron turns #12016 Closed already (2026-10-24)
Inbound-only email channels without SMTP PR #12003 In review — lowers the bar for read-only mailbox access

Roadmap signals:

  • Goal Mode V1 is being staged as a 12-part proposal series; #11879 is "proposal 2/12" and is deliberately dormant (config + command grammar only, no executable behavior). Expect Goal Mode to land across multiple releases, not in v0.8.7.
  • Session event history (#11921, size:XL) proposes append-only canonical session events for effect-safe replay — an architectural change, not a point feature.
  • Persistent memory parity (#8891) remains the headline roadmap commitment.
  • Messaging breadth: XMPP/Prosody with optional OMEMO (#11847) signals continued demand for self-hosted/federated transports.

Prediction: v0.8.7 ships with the SOP/gateway/security fixes above and likely no new features. v0.9.0 scope is coalescing around plugin-install robustness (#11792), send_via attachments (#11997), context-window semantics (#12017), and continued memory work (#11663, #8891).

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points, ranked by evidence strength:

  1. Memory is not yet trustworthy. The tracker with the most engagement (#8891, 12 comments, 3.5 months old) plus an S0 concurrent-write data-loss bug (#10797) and a superseession-scoring defect (#11663 — BM25 normalization can assign 1.0 to unrelated rows, causing consolidation to soft-hide them) all point at the same unmet need: reliable, non-destructive long-term recall.
  2. Platform/locale edge cases bite hard. The PowerShell @ regression (#12005) makes an entire allowlisted workflow unusable on Windows — a case of security hardening breaking legitimate operators. Similarly, provider config gaps silently degrade into locally-rejected turns (#12014).
  3. Opaque security refusals frustrate operators. #11799 explicitly asks for why a command was denied, plus an operator-configurable hint. This is a usability complaint about the security layer, not a request to weaken it.
  4. Email remains second-class. Send-side cannot attach files at all since #9993 (#11996), and inbound-only mailboxes could not even be expressed (#12003). Users are pushing email toward production-grade parity.
  5. Attribution/responsiveness is a positive signal. #12016 closed within 24 hours; #12009 (CI-breaking advisories) closed the same day it was filed; #10066 and #11932 (both high-risk) closed today. Dissatisfaction in this window is about capability gaps, not maintainer neglect.

Use cases visible in the data: embedding ZeroClaw as a library inside a larger binary (hooks, #12016); Windows-native shell automation with mail CLIs; OpenAI-compatible self-hosted/third-party endpoints with unusual context sizes; read-only compliance mailboxes; federated chat via XMPP.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention, ordered by risk × staleness:

Item Age Why it matters
#8891 — Persistent memory parity tracker ~3.5 months (created 2026-07-09) Highest-engagement item; snapshot is dated 2026-08-29 and is now ~8 weeks stale. Needs a refreshed status table.
#10797 — Markdown backend data loss (S0) ~6 weeks (2026-09-12) S0 with no linked fix PR. Longest-lived severe open bug in the dataset.
#9420 — Anthropic stored OAuth profiles ~3 months (2026-07-26) Size:XL, risk:high, trusted contributor; touches core/provider/gateway and security domain. High-value, high-review-cost — likely starved for reviewer bandwidth.
#10446 — Reject tool-call envelopes leaked into prose ~2 months (2026-08-29) domain:security, risk:high, size:XL; describes intermittent production occurrences on gpt-5.6/codex. Merges cleanly per author — blocked on review, not conflicts.
#11422 — TUI signing bound to config-owned key ~3 weeks (2026-10-02) size:XL, blocked on #11411/#11576; #12013 was extracted from it as a smaller testable slice — good unblocking pattern worth continuing.
#11853 — npm audit failure (bot) 6 days Recurring automated security findings need a triage/rotation policy, not one-off fixes.
#11792 — orphaned plugin install stage dirs 9 days Tagged v0.9.0 with no linked PR; a small, self-contained fix that would clear a known disk-leak class.

Backlog health verdict: the 47-open / 3-closed PR ratio is the most important structural number in this digest. Several large, high-risk PRs (#9420, #10446, #11422, #11921) are technically ready but review-bound, while quick wins (#12007, #12013, #11997) move. The bottleneck is review capacity on XL/risk:high changes, not contributor supply.
